title: SEBASTOPOL CEMETERY WALK
location: Robinson road, Robinson road, Sebastopol, CA, 95472, United States
description:
Dare to wander into Sebastopol’s past-where history whispers from the shadows. Tickets are now available for the 23rd annual Cemetery Walk, hosted by the Western Sonoma County Historical Society. This year’s Cemetery Walk is being held on Friday, October 2nd and Saturday, October 3rd . There are 4 walking tours each night offering 4 starting time slots and 1 sit down performance on Saturday inside at the St. Stephen’s Episcopal Church sanctuary.
The evening begins at the Church parking lot. From there, cemetery guides, accompanied by the spirited Hubbub Band, will escort guests to the Historic Burbank Cottage to meet Luther Burbank himself! Guides will then lead you through the Experiment Farm to the Sebastopol Memorial Lawn where you’ll move through the grounds vignette by vignette — six evocative performances, each revealing a story long resting beneath the headstones. Sturdy shoes and flashlights are advised! This year guests will visit and hear the stories of : William Hair, Honoria Toumey, Etta and Mark Hall, Celesta Imogene Faulker, The Smith Family and the Cemetery itself. After the walking tour you will head back to the Luther Burbank Historic Cottage for a brief tour inside and then guides will escort guests back to the Church Hall where a delightful dessert will be prepared and served by the high schools Culinary Arts program headed by Sarah Piccolo. There will be other surprises as well. The sit down performance on Saturday will also enjoy dessert in the hall. Tickets for the event can be found this year on the Society’s website www.wschs.org under the calendar of events page. The cost is $50 and all proceeds go to the Western Sonoma County Historical Society to manage the programs and properties of the Luther Burbank Experiment Farm and the West County Museum.

description: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a year-round Saturday tradition in Sonoma County, bringing together local farmers, ranchers, food artisans, and neighbors from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. This is not just a place to shop, it's a place to connect directly with the people who grow your food. As a Slow Food Sonoma County award recipient, the market prioritizes integrity, seasonality, and true farm-to-community relationships. Expect peak-season produce harvested just hours before market, pasture-raised meats, fresh flowers, artisan breads, handcrafted goods, and thoughtfully prepared foods that reflect the region's agricultural richness. Visitors can stroll the vibrant open-air market, sample local flavors, and experience Sonoma County's food culture in its most authentic form. Families, chefs, and weekend explorers alike gather here to discover what's growing now and to support small farms that keep our local food system strong. Open every Saturday, rain or shine, the Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a cornerstone of the community and a must-visit stop for anyone wanting to taste, shop, and experience Sonoma County at its freshest.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
location: 1st Street Gallery @ WTRSHD
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

title: Apple U-Pick at Gold Ridge Organic Farms
location: Gold Ridge Organic Farms
description:
**Our popular Apple U-Pick Experiences return for a second year!**

Experience the magic of harvest season at Gold Ridge Organic Farms, where you can hand-select the most flavorful Honeycrisp or Fuji apples straight from our certified organic orchard.

Timed entries from 8:30am. Last orchard entry at 11:30am.

Admission: $8 for adults, $3 for children. Registration required.

U-Pick apples: $4 per pound.

**Apple U-Pick FAQs** 

Do I need a reservation? 

Yes! Please reserve your time slot on our reservation site. Reservations help us ensure everyone has a wonderful experience without overcrowding.  

Can I show up without a reservation? 

We require reservations to maintain our capacity limits and ensure everyone enjoys their visit to the fullest.  

Can I cancel my reservation?  

Absolutely! You can cancel your reservation up to 48 hours before your scheduled time by calling us at 707-823-3100. Please note that cancellations made less than 48 hours in advance will result in forfeiture of the entrance fee. 

Can I bring my dog?  

Dogs are not permitted in the orchard, with the exception of service animals. This policy helps ensure the safety and comfort of all our visitors. 

Can I bring a stroller into the orchard?  

For safety reasons, strollers aren't allowed in the orchard, but you're welcome to leave yours at the check-in area where it will be safe and waiting for you!  

I require mobility accommodations. Can I still pick apples in the orchard?  

Yes. Please call us on 707-823-3110 once you’re made a reservation and we can provide suitable transportation into our orchard.

Why is there an entrance fee?  

The entrance fee helps us maintain our beautiful orchard and keep our experienced staff on hand to ensure everyone has a safe and enjoyable experience. 

How much are the apples?  

Our delicious U-pick apples are $4.00 per pound.  

What variety of apples will we be harvesting?  

You'll be picking either Honeycrisp or Fuji apples (depending on seasonal availability).  

Can I harvest heirloom apples?  

While heirloom apples aren't available for U-pick, we offer many wonderful heirloom varieties for purchase in our Farm Shop.  

Are your apples organic?  

Yes, all our apples are organically grown and certified annually by Oregon Tilth!

title: Hallberg Butterfly Gardens Fall Plant Sale & Fundraiser
location: Hallberg Butterfly Gardens
description:
Hallberg Butterfly Gardens’ Fall Native Plant Sale & Fundraiser is coming up October 2nd & 3rd, from 9:00 am–4:00 pm!

Our nursery focuses on California native plants that support local wildlife and pollinators—especially butterflies and moths. Whether you’re adding a few natives to your garden, creating a backyard wildlife habitat, or looking for host and nectar plants, we’ll have a wide variety to choose from.

Fall is an excellent time to plant California native plants.  This year’s sale will include red-flowering currant, seaside daisy, Douglas iris, Dutchman’s pipevine, western azalea, blue elderberry, tiger lily, hedgerow plants, and much more.

Plant lists organized by bloom time and butterfly and moth host plants will be available at the sale, and our knowledgeable staff will be on hand to help answer questions and help you choose plants for your garden.

Because parking at Hallberg Butterfly Gardens is limited, the plant sale is by appointment.

Reserve a time and view the complete plant list on our website: https://hallbergbutterflygardens.org/our-nursery

After your nursery appointment, you’re welcome to stay and enjoy a self-guided walk through the Gardens.

Your plant purchases support Hallberg Butterfly Gardens and our work creating and caring for habitat for butterflies, moths, pollinators, and other local wildlife.

We hope to see you at the Gardens!

title: Jack London State Historic Park WILD Trail Challenge
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
On Saturdays from Sept. 5 to Oct. 3, Jack London State Historic Park’s WILD Trail Challenge returns for a third year.  This series of five hikes covers every trail in the park for a total of 39.5 miles.  The hikes increase in duration and/or difficulty each week.

Participants can sign up for individual hikes or do them all.

The price for each hike is $15.  The park entry fee of $15 per vehicle is waived for these hikes.  Those who sign up for all five hikes before Sept. 5 save 20 percent and pay only $60.

Hike \# 1 – Historic Trails

September 5, 9 a.m.-12:30 p.m.  

A great way to warm up. This hike explores the historic sites and trails of the park. Navigate both sides of the park to discover Jack London’s Beauty Ranch, London Lake, and the Wolf House ruins.

Easy – moderate hike \(approximately 4.5 miles roundtrip\)

Hike \# 2 – Ancient Redwood

September 12, 9 a.m.-1 p.m.   

Meander through the redwoods and sunny oak woodlands of the park’s three Bridge Trails \(Upper, Lower, and Fallen\). The journey leads to the majestic ancient redwood, fondly known as the Grandmother Tree.

Moderate hike \(approximately 6 miles roundtrip\)

Hike \# 3 – Historic Orchard

September 19, 9 a.m.-1:30 p.m.   

Start Location: Note that this hike does not begin at Jack London State Historic Park

Sonoma Developmental Center

Arnold Dr, Eldridge, CA 95431

Stroll along the blue shores of Fern Lake before reaching the Historic Orchard. Learn about the history of the land and the fascinating fruit-bearing crops that thrive there.

Moderate – Difficult hike \(approximately 7 miles roundtrip\)

Hike \# 4 – Ridge

September 26, 9 a.m-3:30 p.m.   

Details: Hikers will gain elevation and an appreciation for the diverse habitats found within the park. They’ll also traverse part of the ever-growing Bay Area Ridge Trail.

Difficult hike \(approximately 12 miles roundtrip\)

Hike \# 5 – Summit 

October 3, 9 a.m.-2:30 p.m.     

A trek to the park summit is the perfect way to complete the WILD Trail Challenges.  Climb Sonoma Mountain to enjoy stunning views, celebrate with fellow hikers, and become a WILD One.

Difficult hike \(approximately 10 miles roundtrip\)

title: Park Rx—Intermediate Hiking for Fitness Fall 2026
location: Sugarloaf Ridge State Park
description:
The program leaders will guide you on 8 weekly hikes with the challenge increasing each week. Leaders will have group discussions about gear, hydration, hiking poles, first aid and pacing, etc. The group's final hike aims for Bald Mountain, where hikers can enjoy stunning vistas.

The following is a list of possible routes specifically selected for this hiking series: 

1) Sat 9/26 — Creekside + Waterfall loop, 3.6 miles, 750 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 2) Sat 10/03 – Vista Trail loop, 3.4 miles, 830 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 3) Sat 10/10 – Hillside to Neptune table + Meadow, 4.4 miles, 970 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 4) Sat 10/17 – Goodspeed to Nattkemper bench, 3.8 miles, 1,240 ft elevation \[meet @ Goodspeed lot\] 5) Sat 10/24 – Hillside + Vista Trail loop, 3.6 miles, 1,070 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 6) Sat 10/31 – False Lake Meadow & Lake Ilsanjo loop in Trionne-Annadel SP, 6.1 miles, 670 ft elevation \[meet @ Annadel's Cobblestone Trailhead\] 7) Sat 11/07 – Fern Lake + Orchard loop in SDC/Jack London SHP, 5.5 miles, 1,460 ft elevation \[meet @ Walnut & North St inside SDC; park on Grove St\] 8) Sat 11/14 – Bald Mtn summit (w/optional Headwaters detour, 5.8 miles), 5.1 miles, 1,670 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\]

Please note these routes are subject to change based on the group and weather, as the group does hike in light rains. Wear appropriate footwear for rocky or slippery trails, and layers. Bring water, and if desired, a snack. The group will be limited to 35 participants. 

The hiking series costs $80 (plus a $10 parking fee per visit. Note that the Sugarloaf Annual Pass is $59 and valid at Sugarloaf and Jack London SHP), or free-of-cost for participants with a September 2026 or newer Park Rx from a Sonoma County Medical Provider.

title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Newcomer Meeting
location: Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Marin
description:
**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits. 

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on first, second and fourth **Saturdays of the month from 9:45 - 10:15 AM at** ​**Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Marin, 240 Channing Way, San Rafael CA 94903**. Contact: Sue M. 415-298-6792​. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan. 

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

**Visit:** https://www.northbayoa.org/

**Find a meeting:** https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

title: "Paddle The Petaluma: Turn to The River" Guided Kayak Tour
location: The Floathouse Petaluma
description:
Paddle the Petaluma: Turn to The River is a relaxed, beginner-friendly guided kayak tour exploring the past, present, and future of Petaluma’s historic waterway. Launching right from downtown at The Floathouse Petaluma, you'll take part in this Sonoma County Signature Experience by spending about 90 minutes on the water in stable sit-on-top kayaks, traveling a gentle mile-and-a-half route through “Petaluma’s Longest Park.”

Along the way, you’ll raft up at docks around town, fascinating  landmarks, and riverfront gathering spaces to hear stories about how this Gold Rush-era “saltwater highway” helped shape Petaluma—and how today’s community is continuing to reinvent and reconnect with the river. This isn’t just a history tour. You’ll also learn about the people, businesses, artists, nonprofits, and river advocates helping shape the waterway’s future right now.

Everything is included in the $75 experience: kayak, gear, knowledgeable local guides, insider river stories, and post-paddle perks at nearby businesses. Finish with plenty of time for brunch, coffee, shopping, or simply hanging out downtown by the water. No experience necessary.

Note: The Floathouse Petaluma is a nonprofit project dedicated to “putting butts in boats and smiles on faces” by offering year-round easy access to the Petaluma River in and on people-powered water craft through rentals, events, classes, lessons and summer camps.

The Napa Valley Museum Yountville has exciting exhibits including Mary Blair: Mid-Century Magic, a special exhibition by the Walt Disney Family Museum exploring the creative vision and achievements of one of Walt Disney’s most imaginative and renowned designers and art directors. Mary’s work appeared in classic Disney animated films like Cinderella \(1950\), Alice in Wonderland \(1951\), and Peter Pan \(1953\). The exhibit closes October 25, 2026, so it might be your last chance to make it before it’s gone!

Bank of America Museums on Us program offers FREE weekend general admission on the first full weekend of every month to Bank of America, Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank credit and debit cardholders. title: Start With What & Why: A Procrastinator's Guide to Stop Overthinking
description:
Start With What & Why: A Procrastinator's Guide to Stop Overthinking

Feeling stuck in the endless loop of overthinking and procrastination?

You’ve accomplished a lot. So why does it feel like something is still missing?

It’s taken me decades to get honest about what I really wanted to do with the rest of my life. It doesn’t have to take you that long.

If you’re an ambitious overthinker, tired of knowing what to do and still not doing it, this session is built for you.

In one hour, we’ll work through three things together, live:

• Why you feel stuck \(and why you’re not broken\)

• What you actually want, and why it matters to you

• One real next step, named and written down before you leave

No fluff. No 20-step system. Just honest, practical work you can use the same day.

I am A Guide You Can Trust

I’ve been in the trenches of personal growth, recovery, and business for decades. I understand what it feels like to be at rock bottom, and I also know the sweetness of victory.

The greatest and most lasting victories in my life are the internal ones. The shifts that rewired how I think, believe, and act. The habits I resisted kicking and screaming, and finally had no other choice but to let go of if I wanted to grow.

Some call them bad habits. Some call them sins. I call them human.

This is how I coach. This is what I teach. And it comes from a place of care, because I’ve been there.

35 Years In. Still Doing the Work.

• 35\+ years in sales and marketing, 80%\+ client retention rate

• 40\+ years of sobriety and personal recovery

• 7 books written and published

• Awards from the New York Times / RMG: Salesperson and Employee of the Year

• Past President, Toastmasters of Petaluma · Past President, Redwood Writers

• 2025 Recipient, Jack London Award for Service to Redwood Writers

• Certified NLP Practitioner & Life Coach

Results and accolades don’t tell the whole story. The real credential is this: I’m still doing the work. Still growing. Still getting humbled. Still showing up.

This Might be for You if:

• You’re successful on the outside and quietly restless on the inside

• You’re tired of knowing what to do and still not doing it

• You’re leading others while secretly running empty

• You’re done with surface-level advice that doesn’t stick

• You’re ready to stop going it alone

You already know what to do. You simply have to be bold enough to become willing to take your first step forward.

If you’re ready, don't wait, register today.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: Color Lab with Lena Wolff
location: Petaluma Arts Center
description:
Color Lab was designed for everyone interested in learning how to experiment with color in new ways. Structured to convey the basics of color theory through hands-on practice, the workshop walks through a sequence of fun, approachable exercises in paint-mixing and collage. In-between art activities, a slideshow is presented that shares information on the biology of color vision, a breakdown of the essential properties of color, and the wondrous phenomenon of color relativity, with visual examples from the early color theorists, textiles, folk-art, and work by contemporary artists.

By the end of the workshop, participants will leave with a small set of color charts and collages, and fodder for a lifetime of future experimentation. 

Open to absolute beginners, practicing artists, designers, and craftspeople alike. Older teens with a serious interest in art are also welcome to register.

$195- Member/$200-Non-member \( includes materials\). 14 students max.

--

Lena Wolff is a Bay Area–based artist, craftswoman, and democracy activist whose work draws from folk traditions, geometric abstraction, and social practice, spanning drawing, collage, sculpture, and public projects. In 2017, she founded Art for Democracy, a nationally recognized initiative promoting civic engagement through art. Her work has been exhibited widely and is held in major collections including the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art and Berkeley Art Museum. She lives in Berkeley with her wife, artist Miriam Klein Stahl, and their daughter.

Main website: www.lenawolff.comArt for Democracy website: https://www.art-for-democracy.org/Workshops: https://lenawolff.com/shop

title: 24th Annual California Jug Band Festival
location: Lagunitas Brewing Company
description:
The 24th Annual California Jug Band Festival Brings a Century-Old American Musical Tradition to Petaluma

Free all-ages music festival at Lagunitas Brewing Company features five California jug bands and an open community jam.

PETALUMA, CA — The California Jug Band Association is bringing  the 24th Annual California Jug Band Festival to Petaluma for the first time on Saturday, October 3, with a full day of free music celebrating one of America’s most distinctive and often-overlooked musical traditions.

The 2026 lineup brings together jug band musicians from throughout California, including groups from the North Bay, East Bay, and Santa Cruz area. While the participating bands perform in a variety of musical styles throughout the year, each will be leaning into its jug band repertoire for the festival.

12:00–1:10 PM — The Trolley Drops, Santa Cruz, CA

1:30–2:40 PM — Paradise Park Jug Band, Santa Cruz, CA

3:00–4:10 PM — Rivertown Skifflers, Petaluma, CA

4:30–5:40 PM — Washboard Rhythm Co., Berkeley, CA

6:00–7:10 PM — Five Cent Coffee, Oakland, CA

7:15–8:00 PM — Open Public Jug Band Jam

EVENT INFORMATION

24th Annual California Jug Band Festival

Saturday, October 3, 2026

12:00–8:00 PM

Lagunitas Brewing Company

1280 N. McDowell Blvd.

Petaluma, CA

Free admission; donations welcome

All ages

No registration required for attendance

From noon to 8 p.m., five California jug bands will perfoarm at Lagunitas Brewing Company, 1280 N. McDowell Blvd., Petaluma. The festival will feature The Trolley Drops, Rivertown Skifflers, Paradise Park Jug Band, Washboard Rhythm Co., and Five Cent Coffee. Admission is free, with donations to the California Jug Band Association’s general fund welcomed throughout the day.

The festival is an all-ages celebration of jug band music—a musical tradition built around community, improvisation, and making music with whatever is at hand. Washboards, washtub basses, kazoos, harmonicas, jugs, and other improvised instruments are as fundamental to the sound as more conventional instruments.

“Jug band music is about as unpretentious as music gets,” said Jared Emerson-Johnson, President of the California Jug Band Association’s board of directors. “It grew out of communities where people made music with what they had, and it became this incredibly creative and joyful tradition. There’s something wonderful about bringing that spirit into an art loving place like Petaluma, where the whole community can come together, listen, dance, have a beer, and maybe even pick up an instrument and join the jam.”

“We love that this festival gives us a chance to see each other and reconnect with the larger jug band community in California,” said Mary McGown, secretary of the California Jug Band Association. “It’s a pretty unusual thing to have this much jug band music in one place, played by so many of the musicians who love this tradition. And then at the end of the day, everybody gets to play together.”

The festival will conclude with an open Jug Band Jam from 7:15 to 8 p.m., inviting musicians and members of the public to join in. Dancers and listeners are welcome throughout the day, and informational stations will offer attendees an opportunity to learn more about the history of the musical tradition.

The full Lagunitas Brewing Company kitchen and taproom will be open during the festival, and on-site parking will be available in the brewery’s regular parking area. Covered space will be available in the event of rain.

All proceeds raised through festival donations will support the California Jug Band Association’s ongoing work to promote and preserve jug band music, fund future festivals, and support additional community music events. The organization hopes eventually to expand its activities to include satellite jug band festivals and gatherings throughout California.

title: Monica Da Silva
location: Bacchus Landing
description:
Monica da Silva grew up living between The United States and Belém, Brazil, a city on the Amazon River. A love of travel and foreign language helped to forge her unique sound. 

 

Paralleling her life, da Silva's music contains an eclectic mix of Brazilian and American influences. Her sound can be classified as International Fusion, as it is heavily influenced by Brazilian music, namely Bossa Nova, but also incorporates elements of Lounge, Electronica, Indie Pop, and Worldbeat. Da Silva brings her cultural diversity to her songs, smoothly flowing between English, Portuguese, and Spanish.

 

In 2010, da Silva released her album "Brasilissima" . The record featured songs in both of her native languages - English and Portuguese. The first single "Aí Então", “was chosen by Putumayo World Music to be included on their compilation “Brazilian Beat”. The upbeat, psychedelic track "That's Not The Way" was chosen by the music director of ESPN to be played during the programming of The FIFA World Cup in 2014, alongside major recording artists Coldplay, Sérgio Mendes, Pitbull, Jennifer Lopez, The Black Eyed Peas, Stan Getz, and Astrud Gilberto. 

Da Silva's single "Soldado de Amor" \(2017\) has been featured in the BBC One series "The Replacement”, in the Paramount Network series "American Woman", and in a 2019 campaign for the designer Tory Burch.

Her music has also been featured in the series "Heartland", and in an ad for Patron Tequila. She is currently recording a new, full-length solo album, as well as writing and recording with her project, Complicated Animals.

title: OAEC Garden Tour
location: Occidental Arts and Ecology Center, 15290 Coleman Valley Rd, Occidental, CA, 95465, United States
description:
Join us for a guided tour of the Occidental Arts & Ecology Center’s demonstration gardens and living landscapes. Led by rotating OAEC staff, these tours offer an opportunity to explore our diverse food, medicinal, pollinator, and native plant gardens while learning about the ecological principles that guide our work. 
When: Tours start at 1pm every first and third Saturday of the month, April through October. 
Where: Tours start and end at the OAEC Nursery. 15290 Coleman Valley Rd, Occidental, CA 95465. Upper Driveway. 
Important Information:
No registration required—just show up!
Please use the second driveway and park in the upper lot near the greenhouses.
The tour route includes steep hills and unpaved dirt and gravel paths. Sturdy shoes, a brimmed hat, and weather-appropriate layers are recommended.
If you require mobility support or have other accessibility needs, please call ahead so we can accommodate you. Monday–Friday, contact the main office at (707) 874-1557 ext. 101. 
A highlight of every tour is the OAEC Nursery, a nonprofit nursery dedicated to uplifting ecologically and culturally important plants. The nursery features a wide selection of perennial food crops, medicinal and native plants, and an ever-evolving collection of annual vegetables and herbs adapted to our region.

title: Dear Evan Hansen
location: Spreckels Center for the Performing Arts
description:
Poignant, raw, and of-the-moment, Dear Evan Hansen pulls back the curtain on the profound desire for human connection in the digital age, offering an empathetic look at the alienation of young people navigating modern social pressures.

The story follows Evan, a high school senior struggling with severe social anxiety who writes motivational letters to himself as a therapeutic exercise. When a troubled classmate dies by suicide with one of Evan’s letters in his pocket, the boy's grieving parents mistakenly believe Evan was his secret best friend. Desperate to comfort them, Evan plays along, spiraling into a web of fabricated emails and internet fame before he must ultimately face the truth.

Powered by a critically acclaimed pop-rock score and the sweeping anthems, Dear Even Hansen is a powerful reminder that we are never truly alone. Spreckels is proud to present the North Bay premiere of this six-time Tony Award winning musical!

location: The California
description: An unforgettable evening presented by the Safari West Zoological Society, supporting the extraordinary animals in our care. Meet the remarkable animals of Safari West and discover the stories behind their names VIP: $450 per person | $350 per person WHAT TO EXPECT Celebrate Our Stars is not a traditional gala. From the moment you arrive, you will become part of an immersive journey through Safari West—filled with special animal encounters, small-group adventures, and plenty of time with the remarkable animals we have come together to celebrate. title: Haunted Wine Tour & Tasting
location: Buena Vista Historical Winery
description:
This fall, Buena Vista Winery invites you to uncover the mysteries, legends, and ghostly encounters woven into more than 165 years of history. Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.

title: S.R. Laws -  Original Acoustic Songwriter
location: Ferry Taproom
description:
S.R. LAWS IS OUT THERE: He approaches songwriting with a passion for songs that we all grew up on. His sound rings a familiar bell in your head while still delivering ideas completely unique. He draws inspiration from outstanding storytellers like John Hiatt, Lou Reed, Steve Earle, Neil Finn and Ron Sexsmith. All of their music and others have carved a deep groove.

Growing up out there in Northern California, he developed a unique connection to music early on. His father worked as a trash collector, and he would spend hours sifting through bags of discarded 45 records. Each find felt like stumbling upon hidden treasures. Some records were covered in dirt and grime, while others were pristine. The thrill of discovering new sounds was exhilarating, and he could hardly wait to drop the needle and immerse himself in the music.

He embarked on a pilgrimage to Texas with just two suitcases and $500 in his bank account. His goal was to dive into the vibrant music scene and learn from fellow songwriters. Austin, known as the "Live Music Capital of the World," offered countless opportunities for him to grow as an artist. Open mics and songwriters' nights became his training ground, where he soaked up every moment, listening to others share their stories through music.

These days, he resides in Sonoma County, California, working hard as a touring artist and singer-songwriter for his original rock band, The Heartsleeves. He invites everyone to join him on this musical journey, sharing his songs one person at a time in this vast and unpredictable world we live in.

title: Gravenstein Mandolin Ensemble
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental
description:
Experience the bright, shimmering sound of strings in harmony as the
Gravenstein Mandolin Ensemble
takes the stage at Occidental Center for the Arts. This talented local ensemble brings together mandolins, mandolas, mandocello, and guitar for a lively musical journey spanning folk traditions, classical favorites, contemporary arrangements, and melodies from around the world.
With the mandolin family’s distinctive blend of warmth, sparkle, and rhythmic energy, the ensemble creates a sound that is both intimate and wonderfully full. Join us for an afternoon of beautiful music, community, and the irresistible charm of many mandolins making music together!
Get Tickets
The Gravenstein Mandolin Ensemble
was formed in 2006 in Sebastopol, California, a town famous for its Gravenstein apples. With humble beginnings, the six original members grew to its present size of fifteen, including the entire mandolin family: mandolins, mandolas, mandocellos, with additional support from guitar and bass. The repertoire includes music from the Classical Era to the most contemporary works for modern mandolins; the geographical range includes music from Italy, Spain, Germany, Eastern Europe as well as Latin America. Smaller groups, or “breakout” ensembles, often perform a variety of music, including Bluegrass, Celtic, Choro, and more. The GME has performed at the Green Center at Sonoma State University, the San Francisco Mandolin Festival and numerous venues through the North Bay Area. In 2018, the GME co-hosted the national convention of the Classical Mandolin Association of America, held in Santa Rosa.

title: Senderos & RFO: Observación de Estrellas
description: ¡Ven a conocer más acerca de nuestro universo!  Milo Buitrago-Casas, físico investigador en el Laboratorio de Ciencias Espaciales de la Universidad de California, Berkeley, nos guiarán en una charla en español acerca de nuestro lugar en el cosmos, mientras que los docentes del Observatorio Robert Ferguson (ubicado dentro de Sugarloaf Ridge State Park) nos guiarán en el uso de telescopios para que tu y tu familia puedan observar el cosmos. El evento comenzará a las 7:00 pm en el aula del Observatorio con una presentación. Milo Buitrago-Casas nos pregunta, ¿qué pasaría si mañana una civilización de otro planeta nos contactara y nos pidiera nuestra ubicación en el Universo para venir a visitarnos? ¿Qué le responderíamos? La respuesta nos lleva en un viaje que empieza donde estamos parados y termina en los límites del universo conocido, qué tan pequeños somos frente a todo lo demás, y por qué esa pequeñez, lejos de asustarnos, es una de las ideas más hermosas que nos ha dado la ciencia.EntradasLa admisión es $10 para adultos, $5 para jóvenes entre 12 y 18 años (deben ser acompañados por un padre de familia o guardián legal), y gratis para menores de 12 años. Obtén tus boletos en rfo.simpletix.com Si posees una tarjeta de EBT, el dueño y tres familiares pueden registrarse por gratis a través del programa Museums for All. Regístrate por adelantado ya que el espacio es limitado y se llenará pronto. Recomendamos vestirse en capas, traer agua, una linterna pequeña de mano (sólamente para aluzar el camino; no puede ser usada cerca del Observatorio a menos que tenga un filtro rojo)  y si la tienes, una guía a las estrellas. Nos reuniremos en el estacionamiento del Granero Blanco. El estacionamiento, usualmente $10, es gratis para este evento.  Para más información, manda un correo electrónico a Alma en senderos@sonomaecologycenter.org o llama al 707-247-5767, martes a sábado entre 9:00 am-5:00 pm. Condiciones lluviosas cancelan el evento pero continuará en condiciones nubladas .Facilidad de acceso: el Observatorio Robert Ferguson se ubica dentro de Sugarloaf Ridge State Park. El área de estacionarse cuenta con un espacio designado para camionetas que necesitan acceso y aunque no oficialmente, hay mucho estacionamiento que puede ser accesible en esa misma área y en el estacionamiento del granero blanco. Hay una rampa que oficialmente cumple con los requerimientos de la Ley para Estadounidenses con Discapacidades (ADA) para ingresar al observatorio. El área de asentamiento en el aula principal del observatorio está compuesto de sillas que fácilmente pueden moverse. Hay baños disponibles dentro del edificio, incluyendo uno accesible. El telescopio de la sala oeste tiene una rampa portátil para alcanzar el ocular, y el telescopio de la sala este es una pantalla grande instalada en la pared.  Encuentra más oportunidades recreacionales a través del programa Senderos Naturales en ésta página.Para aprender más acerca de RFO, visita rfo.org. Para más eventos en Sugarloaf, visita sugarloafpark.org/events

description:

**Time:** Doors 6 PM | Show 8 PM

**Tickets:** $35

**Food Vendor:** TBA

What do people want when they go see a live band? The members of SF Bay Area based tribute band ILLEAGLES believe that everyone in the crowd wants to be engaged and captivated from the first note until the show is done. Over the past year and a half of sold out performances, that is exactly what every crowd has gotten.

ILLEAGLES was founded in late 2016 when 6 friends came together who all had 2 things in common: 1) they loved the music of the Eagles, and 2) each member was an amazing musician in their own right. This common vision led to hours and hours of studying, rehearsing, and mastering each of the Eagles classic hits.

From rockers Life in the Fast Lane and Heartache Tonight, to swooning ballads Desperado and Best of My Love, ILLEAGLES not only reproduce the soaring guitars, multi-part harmonies and tightness of the original band, but also add their own brand of swagger and energy that keeps fans coming back over and over. It's commonplace for a majority of the audience to start singing along on the first song, and continuing to sing until the show is over (or they lose their voices).

ILLEAGLES- A high energy, unforgettable party that leaves fans wanting more...

title: Lou Hazel
location: The Lost Church
description:
Lou Hazel was born in the town of Olean, New York to a family of northeastern wiseacres.

Not one to commit, he skirted the compulsive hunting and fishing tradition held close to his father’s heart - instead cultivating a sensitivity more suited to artists and vagabonds. As a result, his travels brought him across the country and eventually through debilitating depression before coming to rest with a sense of personal peace and positivity in Durham, NC.

Yet, Lou’s brain is still a bat cave. Mostly, he wakes up with no idea what he’s going to do next, then finds himself there. In songwriting, he pulls from this cave rambling, heartfelt tales flowing through unselfconscious truth. In illustrations, he swirls and meanders towards an eventual finish only understood upon completion – as in his music. And in his photography and design work, he renders the essence of fellow musicians into expressive, personalized works of art.

Today, Louie continues crafting genuine folk tales of honest longing, disquieting loss, and nostalgia through a brilliant sheen of fresh insight with humble humor. Grabbing us by the ears in a new-age, Prine-like grip. Transforming the minutiae of everyday life into ever more evocative music. And surprising us all, including himself, with where we emerge.

In other words, Lou Hazel is coming out of this unbearable, unbelievably tragic, disconcerting year like a damn newborn moth with jet engine wings aimed toward a totally full super-moon. And it is good.

You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

OA is not a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two ofrendas in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.

Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures.  An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.

The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

The Community Ofrenda will be a shared, participatory offering. Visitors, locals, volunteers, Board members, and employees can contribute a small photograph, written name, memory, drawing or message honoring someone who has passed away – including a beloved pet. 

The installation will grow throughout October as more people participate.  Materials will be available at the display for visitors who would like to join the celebration and contribute a name, memory or even a drawing of their loved one.

title: Petaluma River History Paddle
location: The Floathouse Petaluma
description:
Enjoy a uniquely Petaluma experience on the water. This two-hour, gentle guided kayak tour launches from The Floathouse Petaluma and explores the river that once served as the region's "saltwater highway." Long before roads and railways, the Petaluma River powered San Francisco, the Gold Rush miners, and even global markets with the produce from local farms and industries, supplying everything from eggs to overalls.

Designed and led by a Petaluman, actor and former history teacher this entertaining and enlightening tour brings history to life through storytelling enhanced by costumed actors on shore. You'll hear fascinating stories from the perspectives of long-ago Petalumans—young workers, entrepreneurs, and colorful characters whose daily lives revolved around the river.

Paddle in stable sit-on-top kayaks through and beyond Petaluma's charming downtown, while gaining a deeper appreciation for how this tidal waterway shaped the city and the region. Visitors are often surprised by how much they learn—and many come back with friends.

$75 per person, all-inclusive. No paddling experience necessary. All equipment provided.

BODY PRAYER IS A FACILITATED EVENT DEVOTED TO INQUIRY INTO EMBODIED CONSCIOUSNESS THROUGH MOVEMENT. 
This class is offered every Sunday morning, and led by Zuza Engler or another teacher. It is usually attended by a vibrant & diverse bunch of welcoming and friendly people, some of whom have practiced Soul Motion® for years, while some ~ never before. 
What to expect 
Guidance and structure are part of every week’s class as we travel across the four landscapes of Soul Motion®:
Dance Infinite (prayer space)
Dance Community (ensemble)
Dance Communion (duet)
Dance Intimate (solo) 
Practices, structures, and points of view are offered to facilitate the journey. Participants are invited to travel across all landscapes, not just their favorite one: dancing by oneself, in duet, in ensemble with several people and eventually the whole room, or witnessing in stillness the beauty of another’s or of everyone’s dance. 
Body Prayer offers a place to be safely uncomfortable as we experiment with ourselves and with each other in our awkward and magnificent dance at the edge of possibility. 
No experience necessary! Everyone welcome!

title: Fall in the Garden: Planting and Caring for your California Natives
location: Petaluma Bounty
description:
Join Sonoma County Master Gardeners Dandi Hagler and Kim Jacobs for a workshop on how to care for your California native plants this fall. 

They'll walk through which plants benefit from pruning now versus later in the season, and how to identify plants that are setting seed, which provide valuable food sources for birds and other wildlife. They'll also cover broader plant care guidelines to keep your garden healthy year-round, along with irrigation strategies for newly installed plants. Whether you're adding California natives for the first time or maintaining what you already have, you'll leave with actionable advice on what to do now.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
location: Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    **www.upstairsart gallery.net** 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: Sonoma Valley Museum of Art FREE October 3-4 Bank of America Museums on Us
location: Sonoma Valley Museum of Art
description:
Bank of America cardholders receive free general admission to participating museums nationwide on the first full weekend of each month; this month is October 3-4. 

As a chill settles in the air, Halloween costumes are planned, and leaves crunch on the ground, take a moment this busy fall season to enjoy local culture! The Sonoma Valley Museum of Art has exciting exhibits including brand new installation The Real-Life Art History of M. Louise Stanley, an exhibit sponsored by Bank of America that celebrates a unique Bay Area Figurative artist for her wildly imaginative narratives and distinctly female perspective, shaped by her keen observations of everyday life and setting her apart from her male contemporaries. The exhibit features Sanley’s large-scale acrylic paintings, gouache and watercolor works on paper, sculptural objects, sketchbooks, studies, photos, and notes from her personal archives, showing the artist’s perspective across multiple media forms. 

Bank of America Museums on Us program offers FREE weekend general admission on the first full weekend of every month to Bank of America, Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank credit and debit cardholders. All you need is your Bank of America, Merrill, or Bank of America Private Bank card and picture ID for access. 

Additional participating museums can be found here: https://about.bankofamerica.com/en/making-an-impact/museums-on-us-partner

location: CHANDON
description: The CHANDON Rocks and Ribs Oyster Fest is an epic afternoon, the ultimate garden bash, where sparkling wine meets fresh-shucked oysters and smoky ribs hot off the grill. Tickets include half a dozen fresh Hog Island oysters, perfectly paired with three CHANDON sparkling cuvées, and St. Louis-style ribs fresh off the grill with all the fixings. This is CHANDON at its most festive: outdoors, indulgent, and unmistakably Californian. A 21\+ garden bash that celebrates the season's final act in the grandest way possible. title: Dear Evan Hansen
location: Spreckels Center for the Performing Arts
description:
Poignant, raw, and of-the-moment, Dear Evan Hansen pulls back the curtain on the profound desire for human connection in the digital age, offering an empathetic look at the alienation of young people navigating modern social pressures.

The story follows Evan, a high school senior struggling with severe social anxiety who writes motivational letters to himself as a therapeutic exercise. When a troubled classmate dies by suicide with one of Evan’s letters in his pocket, the boy's grieving parents mistakenly believe Evan was his secret best friend. Desperate to comfort them, Evan plays along, spiraling into a web of fabricated emails and internet fame before he must ultimately face the truth.

Powered by a critically acclaimed pop-rock score and the sweeping anthems, Dear Even Hansen is a powerful reminder that we are never truly alone. Spreckels is proud to present the North Bay premiere of this six-time Tony Award winning musical!

title: Tales of Suspense - 3 Classic Radio Dramas Live on Stage
location: Cloverdale Performing Arts Center
description:
Step back into the Golden Age of Radio as Cloverdale Performing Arts Center presents three unforgettable tales of mystery and suspense, performed live with voice actors, sound effects, and music created before your eyes.

The Monkey's Paw tells the chilling story of a mysterious talisman that grants three wishes—but at a terrible cost. A timeless supernatural thriller that reminds us to be careful what we wish for.

The House in Cypress Canyon follows a newlywed couple whose dream home becomes the setting for an unexplainable and terrifying mystery. As strange events unfold, the line between reality and nightmare begins to blur.

The Maltese Falcon, adapted from the classic detective story, plunges audiences into a world of deception, danger, and intrigue as private investigator Sam Spade searches for a priceless treasure while navigating a web of unforgettable characters.

Join us for an evening of classic radio drama where every sound sparks the imagination and every story keeps you on the edge of your seat.

title: Haunted Wine Tour & Tasting
location: Buena Vista Historical Winery
description:
This fall, Buena Vista Winery invites you to uncover the mysteries, legends, and ghostly encounters woven into more than 165 years of history. Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.

title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Newcomer Meeting in Santa Rosa
location: Christ Church United Methodist
description:
**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits.

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on **Sundays from 4:00 – 5:00 PM** **at Christ Church United Methodist, 1717 Yulupa Ave., Room #4, Santa Rosa**. Contact: Abigail (707) 293-5888. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html .

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan.

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

**Visit:** https://www.northbayoa.org/

**Find a meeting:** https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

title: MT Jones
location: HopMonk Tavern Novato
description:
With a sound that blends the warmth of 60’s and 70’s greats with the texture of modern R&B and jazz, Jones’ music is rooted in timeless songwriting, live instrumentation, and a voice that carries both vulnerability and power. Already being named as an “Artist to Watch for 2026”. Earmilk praised, “Sky’s the limit for this blue-eyed soul meets retro-R&B mastermind“ while Ladgyunn wrote,”Blending ‘60s and ‘70s soul with modern R&B and jazz influences, Jones’ music pairs timeless songwriting and live instrumentation with a voice that balances vulnerability and power.”

MT Jones has gained strong radio and tastemaker support with previous singles including “Punchin’” “Why I Cry” and “I Don’t Understand” receiving airplay across BBC Radio 2, BBC 6 Music, Jazz FM, and BBC Introducing. Jones has been championed by Jo Whiley, and recorded a live session at BBCs legendary Maida Vale Studios earlier this year for broadcast . He has drawn comparisons to Donny Hathaway, Carole King, and D’Angelo, while remaining distinctly his own.  From his beginnings as a teenage busker to touring internationally with longtime friend Jalen Ngonda and supporting Lauryn Hill, Jones’ journey has been shaped by both graft and soul.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
location: 1st Street Gallery @ WTRSHD
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

Nataraja School of Traditional Yoga

[[breathprayeryoga@protonmail.com](mailto:breathprayeryoga@protonmail.com)]([mailto:breathprayeryoga@protonmail.com](http://mailto:breathprayeryoga@protonmail.com/)), 707-235-1413

Fundamental practices for understanding the holistic nature, energetics and Sanskrit yoga philosophy guiding the approach of this comprehensive system. Long time yoga practitioners as well as new students will benefit. Experience the distinction of this system verses other modern yoga/vinyasa practices commonly taught & the traditional & precise use of ujjayi breath as it relates to the Sanskrit parameters, moving with the breath and the importance of the pause. Talasana is a very unique & profound krama initiating & establishing "samasthiti", the steadiness and focus of mind, balanced energy and steadiness of body - with the two feet together, moving from the center, all the major joints and muscles of the body are exercised using arm and hand movements, back bends, side bends, twists, forward bends, squats and balancing foot stretches. The fingers interlaced create a prana circuit as they come together in the repetitive movement over the head. The breath specific movements stretch the diaphragm, psoas, massage the heart and internal organs, clear the lungs, drain the lymphatic system, stimulate the vagus nerve and calm the mind. Energy is created along the spine and central nervous system, and is distributed throughout the nadis and into the entire energy body. Regular practice of Talasana flowers into to ananta samapatti and understanding "stillness in movement".
Class begins with Opening Mantras & Ding Namaskar (Devotional Salutation to the Directional Spheres with Breath & Mantra). Then moves to Tāĺāsana to Savasana then Seated Prānāyāma (Yogic Breathing) including Morning Cleansing Kriyas, Ujjayi, Nadi Shuddi, Samantraka Prānāyāma, Pratyahara, Dharana. May include Specific Mudra (Energetic Bodily Gestures).

title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two ofrendas in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.

Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures.  An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.

The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

The Community Ofrenda will be a shared, participatory offering. Visitors, locals, volunteers, Board members, and employees can contribute a small photograph, written name, memory, drawing or message honoring someone who has passed away – including a beloved pet. 

The installation will grow throughout October as more people participate.  Materials will be available at the display for visitors who would like to join the celebration and contribute a name, memory or even a drawing of their loved one.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: Haunted Wine Tour & Tasting
location: Buena Vista Historical Winery
description:
This fall, Buena Vista Winery invites you to uncover the mysteries, legends, and ghostly encounters woven into more than 165 years of history. Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.

title: Salsa Beginners 2 - Mondays
location: Salsa Dance Marin
description:
Ready to take your salsa to the next level? Salsa lessons in Marin will help you to add some flair and fluidity to your salsa dancing.

Pre-requisite: Salsa Beginners 1 – You know your basic steps, left turn, right turn, cross-body lead, and you hold your frame.

What You’ll Learn

We’ve curated a curriculum designed to build your confidence and your “social dance” vocabulary:

• The Cross Body Lead \(CBL\) Series: Master both Inside and Outside Turns, the essential building blocks for moving your partner across the floor with grace.

• The “I Turn – You Turn”: A classic social dance staple that develops timing and hand-change coordination.

• The Walk-Through: Learn how to transition smoothly through the dance space without breaking your rhythm.

• Footwork & Shine: We’ll break down the footwork pattern that adds personality to your “shines.”

Technique & Artistry

• Dancing is about more than just where your feet go. In this level, we dive deeper into the “how”:

• The Frame: Understand the “tension and compression” needed to lead and follow clearly without using muscle.

• Upper Body Mechanics: Learn how to isolate your ribcage and shoulders to move with that authentic Latin soul.

• Connection: Developing a “heavy” but responsive arm connection to ensure your partner feels every lead.

Important Details

• No dance experience required: Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

• No partner necessary: Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

• Please wear non-marking shoe soles: This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

title: Lavender Labyrinth Sound Bath Experience
location: Bees n blooms
description:
Join us in our most dreamy location yet, in the center of a lavender labyrinth for an exquisite sunset sound Bath Experience!

Join us in our most dreamy location yet, in the middle of lavender labyrinth at sunset!

Mondays through October 6th

We are thrilled to share this magic with you! Let the fragrance of lavender fill and sooth your senses as the sound expands your awareness.

Sound baths create the space for self-healing and transformation. The resonance of the instruments is not just an auditory experience ~ it's like receiving a full body sound massage.

There will be 8 Gongs, Crystal singing bowls, Hand pan, Mono chord, Chimes galore, Ocean drum, Native drum, Angelic Vocals & more.The vibrations will transport you on a powerful healing journey!

PLEASE NOTE: The sound bath starts at 7pm. Gates close at 6:45 PM. Please be Mindful of timing. You will need time to park, walk up and set up. You are welcome to come walk the labyrinth and visit the Farm Stand from 6 pm onward. Please check the hourly weather so you are prepaired. You will be lying on the grass, so please bring all that you will need to feel cozy and warm, "yoga mat" or camping pad, "Blanket" or sleeping bag, a pillow, eye mask, and water bottle. Wonderful Lavender Eye Masks will be available to purchase for $25 by the Bees & Blooms Farm Stand.

If we have environmental Circumstance such as rain or unhealthy air quality due to fires we will postpone to Wednesday of the same week and your tickets will roll over to that day. If these conditions are present it is your responsibility to monitor your emails\(also junk/spam\) for notifications. In these force of nature situations Tickets are not refundable but are transferable! Your understanding and cooperation is greatly appreciated.

Please be informed that there are bee hives on site and there may be bees on the lavender plants. If you are allergic to bee stings, bring your Epipen. An incident is unlikely, but best to be prepared. Also, at some point, probably mid July the Lavender will began to be harvested so there may be less lavender towards the end of the month.Full Bloom occurs mid June. The last sound bath of the Lavender season will be Oct. 6th. The labyrinth & farm will be beautiful however the Lavender will be reaching the end of its cycle around mid. July. You will walk through many rows of a varity of blooming flowers on you way from parking.

Only disability trained Registered Service dogs are permitted because of the animals on the farm and the nature of the Sound Bath. Your understanding is appreciated. Also, please no children under 10 years of age.

Labyrinths represent a metaphor for your life path and the journey you are making. While walking the path of the labyrinth, either alone or with a group, focus on your feelings and emotions to allow you to connect with yourself. You may also want to choose a meditation that you are comfortable with in order to clear and quiet your mind. The uses of a labyrinth are many; relief from stress and anxiety, healing, meditation, problem solving, enhancing intuition, expanding thought processes, communicating with the Divine, balancing mind, body and spirit, letting go of unwanted energies, obtaining goals, celebrating and remembering others, building trust in yourself or others, and coping with grief, sorrow and loss. The labyrinth is an ancient symbol that relates to wholeness. It combines the imagery of the circle and the spiral into a meandering but purposeful path. The Labyrinth represents a journey to our own center and back again out into the world. Labyrinths have long been used as meditation and prayer tools.

Looking forward to sharing this Extraordinary Experience with you! In Gratitude

title: Poetic Medicine: 10/06/2026 — Sebastopol Center For the Arts, California
location: Sebastopol Center for the Arts, 282 S High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472
description:
Poetic Medicine: 10/06/2026

  
    
      
        
          $15.00
        
      
    
  

PLEASE NOTE: October Poetic Medicine will meet on the first Tuesday of October. Tuesday, October 6th, 2026; 4:00 – 5:30pm$15.00Max 20 Attendees, Pre-registration required(We are unable to offer refunds or transfers for this class. If you cannot attend, please consider it a donation. Thank you!)The practice of “poem making” offers a means to express the metaphors and meaning of the joys and suffering we experience in ourselves and bear witness to in others. Poetry can be a salve for the heart and soul. It is a way of speaking what is true in our hearts and is often difficult to access without a creative spark. You do not have to be a "poet" or even a "writer" to allow words and feelings to pour through your pen.Redwing Keyssar has been leading "poetic medicine" sessions through her work in Palliative Care at UCSF for the past 5 years. Her work has created an international community of people who, by listening to and writing poetry together, have healed wounds of grief and loss, helped "wounded healers," and provided resiliency to move forward on our life paths.Writing poetry in community is a bit like attending a meditation retreat. The instruction for most beginners when learning to meditate is to simply bring oneself back to the breath, each time the mind wanders. In poem-making, the instruction is to bring oneself back to the heart and along with a deep breath, see if one can open a little bit wider. When we witness each other in this process, in a circle of open-heartedness, something magical happens!This is an IN-PERSON gathering to establish a strong and safe creative community. We are all poets!About the Instructor: Judith Redwing Keyssar, RN has traversed an amazing 35+ year journey in the healing arts/healthcare. Redwing is an educator, end-of-life doula, author, poet, song-writer, ceremonialist, national presenter and frequent contributor to public issues about Palliative and End of Life Care. Redwing is currently the Director of Education at the MERI Center for Education in Palliative Care at UCSF/Mt. Zion. Her professional career includes being the Clinical Director at Zen Hospice Project and the Director of Palliative Care and Nursing at Jewish Family and Children’s Services from 2004-2018. She is a founder and adjunct faculty member of the California State University Shiley/Haynes Institute of Palliative Care, and has taught courses at OLLI at Sonoma State. Redwing is the author of an award-winning book, “Last Acts of Kindness; Lessons for the Living from the Bedsides of the Dying” and is the recipient of numerous awards in the field of Palliative Care. After studying with John Fox at the Institute for Poetic Medicine, her passion for using poetry as a healing modality has led to the development of a successful international program in Poetic Medicine, through her work at the UCSF MERI Center. Learn more about her here: https://redwingkeyssar.com/

1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

description:

·         Buffie Campbell, Vice Chair, Sherwood Valley Rancheria, cultural teacher and master basket maker,

·         Henry Edward Frank, Yurok/Kashaya Pomo, who will show paintings and work with Legos titled Mind Prison,

·         Digital artist Nicolas \(Nico\) Vargas, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians, whose art was featured at the 55th Annual Stanford Powwow.

·         plus Gloria Carretero; Rose Hammock; Rudy Hammock; Jocelyn Garcia; Arella Ortega LaRose, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Angelica Smith, Manchester Point Arena and Yokayo Rancheria; Maria Pasalo; Michelle Napoli; Martina Morgan, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Hands Lopez; Shashoni Hanover-Redenbaugh; Katie Williams-Elliott, Juan Partida, and Mia Pasalo, Big Valley Pomo Tribe.
