title: SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River
location: The Floathouse Petaluma
description:
Slow down and float into a quieter rhythm with SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River at The Floathouse Petaluma. Launching from downtown Petaluma, this peaceful on-the-water yoga experience feels worlds away from the bustle—set in the calm, protected turning basin where the river naturally invites you to relax.

This all-levels, 90-minute session welcomes everyone, from first-time paddle boarders and yoga newcomers to experienced practitioners. We begin with a short, gentle paddle from the docks to get comfortable on your board \(knees are always welcome\), then anchor together so tidal movement won’t interrupt your flow. Once settled, you’re free to move, stretch, rest, or simply be—guided by expert instruction and supported by the shared energy of the group. Evening sessions and morning sessions allow YOU to choose the vibe that suits you best.

All equipment is provided, including extra-stable paddleboards that are wider and longer than a yoga mat, designed to help you feel grounded and secure on the water.

Perfect for locals and Bay Area visitors alike, SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River offers a rare chance to experience downtown Petaluma from the water—peaceful, playful, and deeply restorative.

It’s YOUR river. Come out and play.

title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Newcomer Meeting
location: Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Marin
description:
**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits. 

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on first, second and fourth **Saturdays of the month from 9:45 - 10:15 AM at** ​**Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Marin, 240 Channing Way, San Rafael CA 94903**. Contact: Sue M. 415-298-6792​. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan. 

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

**Visit:** https://www.northbayoa.org/

**Find a meeting:** https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

title: Arboriculture 101 for Homeowners
location: Western Hills Garden
description:
Have you ever brought home a tree from a nursery only for it to die a few months or years later? Or purchased a property with mature trees suffering from sparse canopies or leaning oddly?

 Join WHG's Living Collections Coordinator Kat Gritt to learn tips and resources to support your trees' wellbeing, whether you have a new sapling ready for planting or mature trees on your property.  

This class is meant to give participants knowledge and techniques to make the best nursery selections, properly install trees, and keep them healthy. Kat will cover common landscape tree issues so that participants are better prepared to make decisions about tree placement and horticultural care for a successful home landscape.

Care techniques will be demonstrated on trees in the Western Hills Garden.

title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two ofrendas in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.

Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures.  An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.

The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

The Community Ofrenda will be a shared, participatory offering. Visitors, locals, volunteers, Board members, and employees can contribute a small photograph, written name, memory, drawing or message honoring someone who has passed away – including a beloved pet. 

The installation will grow throughout October as more people participate.  Materials will be available at the display for visitors who would like to join the celebration and contribute a name, memory or even a drawing of their loved one.

description:
Derek Irving channels the raw, unfiltered spirit of early rock ’n’ roll, blending the swagger of 1950s rockabilly with the driving rhythms of 1960s surf and rhythm & blues. The band’s sound is a nod to pioneers like Chuck Berry, Eddie Cochran, and Carl Perkins, but it doesn’t stop there—there’s the grit of Bo Diddley, the twang of Link Wray, and a dash of reverb-soaked surf guitar straight out of a California beach party.

At the heart of every show is Derek’s fiery guitar work—snarling riffs, wild bends, and rapid-fire picking that harken back to rock ’n’ roll’s golden age. Anchoring the groove is the slap and thump of upright bass, a rhythmic heartbeat that gets crowds moving and keeps the energy rolling from the first chord to the last encore.

This isn’t just a throwback—it’s a high-octane revival of the roots of rock ’n’ roll, delivered with a modern edge that pulls fans of all ages onto the dance floor. Whether it’s a winery crowd, a festival stage, or a late-night club, Derek Irving and his band ignite every room with a sound that’s timeless, electric, and impossible to stand still to.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Check out informational tables hosted by Sonoma State University Library, Sonoma County Public Library, National Women’s History Alliance, Sonoma County Historical Society, Saturday Afternoon Club, Sonoma Valley Historical Society and the League of Women Voters for Sonoma County.

Hear from our guest speaker, Molly Murphy MacGregor, Co-Founder of the National Women’s History Association \(NWHA\), and watch the fascinating video by Wild West Women Inc. called "California Women Win the Vote".

It’s a great chance to learn, celebrate, and connect with the history of women’s rights in California. See you there!

Free parking is available in the parking lot behind the barracks.

title: Funky Florals | Cut Paper Collage Workshop with Sally-Ann Langley
location: Petaluma Arts Center
description:
Get ready to play with color, pattern, and shape in this fun, whimsical collage workshop! You'll create your very own Funky Floral artwork using painted papers, colorful patterns, and playful floral and leaf shapes.

You'll make your own painted collage papers, add colorful patterns with paint pens, then get snipping and cutting your flowers and leaves. From there, you'll experiment with composition and arrange your pieces into a funky floral design that's uniquely yours. Create a 9x11 artwork or a collection of notecards and gift tags!

The emphasis is on having fun and playing with your creativity, even if you've never created a collage before. Sally-Ann will demonstrate each step and cheer you on along the way.

About Sally-Ann:

Sally-Ann is a Northern California multidisciplinary artist based in Petaluma, CA. After working for 20 years as a packaging designer, she is now a freelance illustrator and licensed artist selling her work online and on products nationwide. Sally-Ann teaches workshops in the US and internationally.

title: Petaluma River Upstream High Tide Paddle
location: The Floathouse Petaluma
description:
When the tide is high, the Petaluma River opens into a quieter, greener world.

Join The Floathouse crew at their central downtown dock for a gentle, guided paddle upstream, timed to higher tides that allow access beyond the downtown channel and into a tranquil tidal slough. With extra water beneath us, we’re able to glide into calm, lush stretches of the river that are normally out of reach.

This unhurried paddle highlights the natural beauty of the Petaluma River’s brackish, tidal waterway. Watch for great egrets, blue herons, snowy egrets, turtles basking along the banks, and abundant plant life. The calm water and peaceful surroundings create a deeply grounding experience—many guests say they feel their stress melt away within minutes.

Along the way, knowledgeable guides share stories of the river’s ecology and human history, offering insight into how this upper channel has shaped—and continues to shape—Petaluma. It’s a rare opportunity to experience how close wild nature lives to the heart of downtown.

Beginner-friendly. Sit-on-top kayaks and all gear provided.

Join Cana Ranch for its inaugural release party, an intimate harvest gathering celebrating the launch of its first Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon — and a mission to create meaningful employment opportunities for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD).

Founded by husband-and-wife team Tyler and Kelly Mullman, Cana Ranch was created with the belief that wine can be a vehicle for social impact. The brand partners with organizations working to expand employment and job training opportunities for adults with IDD, with the goal of creating a sustainable path to meaningful work through the wine and hospitality industries.

At Cana Ranch Uncorked, guests will gather for an afternoon of wine, food and conversation featuring Cana Ranch winemaker Richard Frederick and seasonal bites thoughtfully curated by Chef Misty Phelps.

The afternoon will include:

A tasting of Cana Ranch’s inaugural **2024 Cabernet Sauvignon**, sourced from Tournahu Vineyard in St. Helena

Select wines from Friends of Cana Ranch

Seasonal bites by Chef Misty Phelps

A silent auction

Remarks from Cana Ranch founders Tyler and Kelly Mullman

An introduction to the **WineBev Services** program and its work creating employment opportunities for adults with IDD

**All proceeds from the event will support United Cerebral Palsy of the North Bay’s WineBev Services program**, which provides employment and job-training opportunities for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

Come raise a glass to Cana Ranch’s first vintage and to a future where great wine can help create greater opportunities for everyone.

**$150 donation**

title: Dear Evan Hansen
location: Spreckels Center for the Performing Arts
description:
Poignant, raw, and of-the-moment, Dear Evan Hansen pulls back the curtain on the profound desire for human connection in the digital age, offering an empathetic look at the alienation of young people navigating modern social pressures.

The story follows Evan, a high school senior struggling with severe social anxiety who writes motivational letters to himself as a therapeutic exercise. When a troubled classmate dies by suicide with one of Evan’s letters in his pocket, the boy's grieving parents mistakenly believe Evan was his secret best friend. Desperate to comfort them, Evan plays along, spiraling into a web of fabricated emails and internet fame before he must ultimately face the truth.

Powered by a critically acclaimed pop-rock score and the sweeping anthems, Dear Even Hansen is a powerful reminder that we are never truly alone. Spreckels is proud to present the North Bay premiere of this six-time Tony Award winning musical!

title: Haunted Wine Tour & Tasting
location: Buena Vista Historical Winery
description:
This fall, Buena Vista Winery invites you to uncover the mysteries, legends, and ghostly encounters woven into more than 165 years of history. Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.

title: Mighty Real: A History of LGBTQ Music: 1969-2000 with Barry Walters!
location: Cadet Wine & Beer Bar
description: Tickets: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/mighty-real-a-history-of-lgbtq-music-1969-2000-with-barry-walters-tickets-1998864880666? Napa Pride presents a deep dive into LGBTQ\+ music history, with world-renowned music writer Barry Walters! Plus DJ Rotten Robbie dance party! Barry Walters's new book, Mighty Real, has earned widespread critical acclaim. He has traveled across the country to promote it, appearing on The Kelly Clarkson Show, morning television programs, popular podcasts, and local bookstores. Barry will read from his book, have a Q&A, a book signing, then DJ Rotten Robbie will spin music from Barry's book for a big ol' gay dance party! Barry Walters has spent 40 years documenting the intersection of mainstream and LGBTQ culture. He began his career at The Village Voice — where he came out publicly in a 1986 Pet Shop Boys review — before becoming a fixture at Spin and Rolling Stone. In 1992, Walters’ work at the San Francisco Examiner made him the first critic to receive an award from The National Gay and Lesbian Journalists Association. Throughout the Nineties, he was The Advocate’s music columnist before a decade’s worth of writing at Out. Along the way, he’s regularly appeared in Entertainment Weekly, NPR, Pitchfork, and other media mainstays. Love Me Like You Should: The Brave and Bold Sylvester, a 2020 mini-documentary he wrote and co-produced for Amazon Music, won a Clio Award. Barry's book will be available for purchase. Event is free, but tickets are encouraged. No-host food and beverage available by our friends at Cadet.

title: SugarShuttle: Sugarloaf ↔ Hood Mtn, Los Alamos Rd
location: Sugarloaf Ridge State Park
description:
**How it works**: Every hour, our Shuttle will leave from either Sugarloaf Ridge State Park's Visitor Center, making a brief stop at the Goodspeed parking lot, or Hood Mountain Regional Park’s Los Alamos Rd parking lot. Make a reservation to ride to the other end of the trail and begin your hike, or hike and ride back. We recommend riding first and hiking back to your car afterward—no worries about how long you take to finish your adventure. The hike should take 4 to 5 hours depending on your pace; the distance is about 7.5 miles one-way with approximately 2,500ft of elevation gain. 

Bring at least 64 oz of water, sun protection (the majority of the trail is exposed), a good paper map (some of the trail signs on Hood Mtn Regional Park are still damaged from the 2020 wildfire and trails might not be well marked), and if desired, hiking poles, a lunch, and a friend.

If you are riding from Sugarloaf, the Goodspeed lot fills up quickly. If it is full, please park at the main lot and pick up the shuttle at the Visitor Center (you will have to hike a mile back to the main lot from the bottom of the canyon/Goodspeed lot). Remember, the Hood Mountain pick-up is at the end of Los Alamos Road: 3000 Los Alamos Rd, Santa Rosa, CA, 94509. Los Alamos Rd is a windy, narrow, sometimes one-lane, 5-mile road without cell reception—allow time to get to the lot (NOT the Pythian Rd lot). Please note there are currently no restrooms, water, or cell service at this trailhead.  

**Registration is required as there is only space for 6 riders at a time**, but you can ride on a space-available basis as well. There is no charge for the ride, the $10 reservation fee is refunded on site the day of the event, unless you choose to donate it to keep this service running. **Dogs and bikes are not allowed in the shuttle or on Goodspeed Trail** (the State Park portion of the hiking route). Parking fees apply.

title: Bhakti Yoga Daytreat
location: Spirit Rock Meditation Center
description:
with Janet Stone

In a world of constant noise, this day is an invitation to return to the wisdom beneath it—to pause, listen deeply, and reconnect with the heart of who you are.

Through meditation, breath, yoga, chanting, music, storytelling, contemplation, time in nature, and rest, we’ll nourish the nervous system while exploring the stories that shape our lives. Drawing from the wisdom of the *purāṇas* (sacred myths), we’ll gently inquire into the narratives we’ve inherited, the ones we’ve unconsciously repeated, and the possibility of living a story that is more awake, courageous, and true.

Bhakti—the yoga of the heart—reminds us that every emotion can become fuel for transformation. Chanting is a love letter to life, inviting us to offer our voices to something greater while awakening our innate capacity for love, grace, resilience, and devotion.

Join Janet Stone for a day of practice, reflection, community, and stillness as we step away from the noise and back toward ourselves.

This program will include a non-heated, vigorous yoga asana practice.  In addition to the vigorous yoga asana practice mentioned above, our day together will involve a **long, strenuous hike** that includes steep sections of both uphill and downhill. You **must be in good physical shape and not require any mobility assistance or devices**, other than a typical trekking pole or stick for this program.

title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Meeting
description:

In OA, members experience spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery by practicing the Twelve Steps and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

Overeaters Anonymous \(OA\) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits. 

We hold an in-person meetings at 9:30 on Sunday mornings at Church of the Nazarene, 18980 Arnold Drive, Sonoma, CA \(a small room directly off of parking lot; look for the sign posted\) and newcomers are always welcome.

You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

OA is not a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does not endorse any specific food plan. 

Visit: https://www.northbayoa.org/

Find a meeting: https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two ofrendas in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.

Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures.  An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.

The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

The Community Ofrenda will be a shared, participatory offering. Visitors, locals, volunteers, Board members, and employees can contribute a small photograph, written name, memory, drawing or message honoring someone who has passed away – including a beloved pet. 

The installation will grow throughout October as more people participate.  Materials will be available at the display for visitors who would like to join the celebration and contribute a name, memory or even a drawing of their loved one.

title: Soul Motion®: Body Prayer every Sunday in person
location: Wischemann Hall, 465 Morris St, Sebastopol, CA, 95472, United States
description:
BODY PRAYER IS A FACILITATED EVENT DEVOTED TO INQUIRY INTO EMBODIED CONSCIOUSNESS THROUGH MOVEMENT. 
This class is offered every Sunday morning, and led by Zuza Engler or another teacher. It is usually attended by a vibrant & diverse bunch of welcoming and friendly people, some of whom have practiced Soul Motion® for years, while some ~ never before. 
What to expect 
Guidance and structure are part of every week’s class as we travel across the four landscapes of Soul Motion®:
Dance Infinite (prayer space)
Dance Community (ensemble)
Dance Communion (duet)
Dance Intimate (solo) 
Practices, structures, and points of view are offered to facilitate the journey. Participants are invited to travel across all landscapes, not just their favorite one: dancing by oneself, in duet, in ensemble with several people and eventually the whole room, or witnessing in stillness the beauty of another’s or of everyone’s dance. 
Body Prayer offers a place to be safely uncomfortable as we experiment with ourselves and with each other in our awkward and magnificent dance at the edge of possibility. 
No experience necessary! Everyone welcome!

title: Workshop: Off the Grid Printing
location: D
description: In this two day workshop, students will work hands-on with metal and wood type to create off-grid compositions-playing with spacing, rotation, fragmentation, overlap, and improvisation. We'll explore how imbalance, disruption, and intuition can shape meaning, rhythm, and visual impact in printed work. This class emphasizes process over perfection. Expect to test ideas, make quick prints, respond to chance, and let the material qualities of type and press guide the work. Suitable for curious beginners and experienced printers alike, this workshop offers a supportive space to experiment, loosen habits, and discover new possibilities in letterpress printing beyond the grid. All materials provided. No prior letterpress experience required, though comfort with basic printing concepts is helpful.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
location: Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: Meet + Greet: More Trouble Than It's Worth by Lisa Moore Ramee
description: Join us for a special meet-and-greet event with Lisa Moore Ramee, author of More Trouble Than It's Worth. This event is free, but we appreciate your RSVP below so we can plan for your attendance. ABOUT THE BOOK "Ramée successfully weaves themes of friendship, sports, social responsibility, and family into this engaging coming-of-age story. Shayla’s journal features quotations from famous Black women, a seamless way of sharing the insights she gains with readers...A lively novel that explores the inner conflicts and group dynamics that tweens often reckon with." — Kirkus Reviews From award-winning author Lisa Moore Ramée comes the companion to A Good Kind of Trouble, a heartfelt and powerful sequel about coming of age, social justice, and the trials of friendship and competition, in which Shayla will learn the true definition of “personal best.” After a hard seventh-grade year full of misunderstandings, face plants, and bullies, all Shayla wants is a hassle-free summer. Her ticket to a summer of fun? Joining the club track team! However, Shayla struggles to fit in with new friends, to set a personal best that will secure her a spot in the exclusive Junior Olympics, and reluctantly earns the title of “Prank Queen.” But Shayla discovers that sometimes trying so hard to stay out of trouble ends up making things a whole lot worse. Will she risk new friendships by owning up to a big mistake? And is she ready to speak out against another social injustice? In this powerful and heartfelt follow-up to A Good Kind of Trouble from acclaimed author Lisa Moore Ramée, Shayla will learn the true definition of personal best. ABOUT THE AUTHOR Lisa Moore Ramée was born and raised in Los Angeles and now lives in Northern California with her husband, daughter, obnoxious cat, and rambunctious \(but sweet\) dog. She's a devout believer in dreams coming true and is the author of A Good Kind of Trouble, a Walter Dean Myers Honor Book, The Everybody Experiment, Something to Say, and MapMaker. You can visit her online at lisamooreramee.com.

description: Callie Watts is a singer/songwriter from Northern California who was raised on classical music, The Beatles and The Beach Boys before discovering Joni Mitchell, Elton John, Stevie Wonder, Paul Simon, Billy Joel, Carole King, and all the great writers of the ’60s and 70’s who have influenced her sound and writing style. After graduating high school, Callie began playing and performing solo, as well as in local and bay area bands of different genres. She’s played blues with Eric Lindell and the Reds, funky soul with Phatty, and jazz/swing with Savoy Swingers along with many other various projects. Callie has taken turns throughout her career as a keyboardist, guitarist, writer, and lead/backing vocalist, and she’s currently a member of the dynamic Sonoma County funk rock band Burrows and Dilbeck, having joined in 2010 as part of the former band Frobeck. Over time, she’s had the honor of opening for acts such as Bootsy Collins, Elvin Bishop, Huey Lewis and The News, War, Ozomatli, Bill Champlin, Booker T, and the B52s. Callie continues to perform frequently as an acoustic solo artist, focusing on developing a core audience and a buzz for her original material. **Unplug and Groove: P-Butta Live at the Vineyard**

Join us for No Cell Sundays with P-Butta, a local powerhouse trio that's been making Sonoma County move for decades.

P-Butta is the instrumental side project of the musicians from Rising Tide, the original Groundation band. With Marcus Urani on keyboards, Ryan Newman on bass, and Paul Spina on drums, this three-piece brings together four decades of funk, soul, and jazz mastery that satisfies any musical palate.

Expect to hear groovy covers from legendary artists like The Meters, Booker T & the M.G.'s, Herbie Hancock, Donnie Hathaway, Cannonball Adderley, and even the Beastie Boys. Whether you're a jazz head or just love good vibes, P-Butta delivers the perfect soundtrack for a Sunday afternoon in wine country.

**What's No Cell Sundays?**

It's simple: disconnect from your devices, reconnect with great wine, live music, and the people around you. *Check your phone with us at the door and receive a complimentary tasting.* Bring a blanket, grab a glass, and spend your Sunday the way it was meant to be spent.

The tasting will be focused on wines from the Russian River Valley. You are welcome to bring snacks to share if you wish. The hostesses will likely bring a something to share as well.

Optional dress code: Everyone wear something that sparkles- Sequins, Glitter, Metallics, Rhinestones, Pink, Sparkly shoes, etc.

The story of Foppiano Vineyards is a family epic full of tradition, perseverance and contributions to the history of Sonoma County and the wine country. Founded in 1896 by Giovanni Foppiano, Foppiano Vineyards is one of Sonoma County’s oldest continually-operated, family-owned wineries. They offer a variety of different wines and a lovely space to enjoy ourselves in.

The tasting fee and gratuity will be $38 per person, with $1 for added for our 'Slush' fund, to pay for incidentals with the club. Spots must be reserved by prepaying, using Paypal through the Meetup website. Paypal does charge a nominal fee for payment processing. We can refund you the price of your tasting fee if you need to cancel and let us know 5 days in advance.

Thanks and we look forward to sharing our favorite wines with you!!

Rachael and Kris

description:
Poignant, raw, and of-the-moment, Dear Evan Hansen pulls back the curtain on the profound desire for human connection in the digital age, offering an empathetic look at the alienation of young people navigating modern social pressures.

The story follows Evan, a high school senior struggling with severe social anxiety who writes motivational letters to himself as a therapeutic exercise. When a troubled classmate dies by suicide with one of Evan’s letters in his pocket, the boy's grieving parents mistakenly believe Evan was his secret best friend. Desperate to comfort them, Evan plays along, spiraling into a web of fabricated emails and internet fame before he must ultimately face the truth.

Powered by a critically acclaimed pop-rock score and the sweeping anthems, Dear Even Hansen is a powerful reminder that we are never truly alone. Spreckels is proud to present the North Bay premiere of this six-time Tony Award winning musical!

title: Sambada
location: HopMonk Tavern
description: While Brazilian natives Papiba Godinho and Dandha da Hora bring their profound knowledge and respect for the roots of afro-brazilian song and dance, the entire band has developed a type of samba-reggae-funk with a universal appeal. SambaDá musically unites the Americas, drawing from percussion based styles of South and Central America, and blends it with that good old funk and reggae back beat so familiar to crowds of North America.  For over ten years, SambaDá has been mixing contemporary sounds with the roots of brazilian culture. Papiba is a master of Capoeira, an Afro Brazilian martial art form created by Brazilian slaves, which draws on music and acrobatic movements. Dandha was born into the rich Afro Brazilian traditions of Salvador, Bahia and the Carnival Group Ile Aiye, and started her dancing career at age 6. Ile Aiye has been in the forefront of Civil Rights in Brazil, promoting equality and justice, and is widely recognized as the first Afro Brazilian BLOCO or group to perform in Brazil's notorious Carnival celebrations.  The other members of SambaDá come from a wide range of styles, generations and sensibilities. What unites this band from such diverse backgrounds is a magic that can be felt by both the band and the audience. SambaDá brings joy to each performance, and keeps their fans asking for more!! SambaDá musically unites the Americas, drawing from percussion-based styles of South and Central American samba and salsa, and blending them with the funk!

title: Songs of the Living Earth
location: Sebastopol Community Cultural Center
description:
Join us for an unforgettable evening of music, community, and celebration as the internationally acclaimed band Curawaka travels from Europe for a rare Northern California performance in Sebastopol.

Rooted in the wisdom traditions of the Earth, Curawaka's music weaves together ancestral songs, indigenous languages, and contemporary artistry into an experience that invites us to remember our deep connection with nature, one another, and the sacred.

The day begins with an opening circle to bring our hearts and minds into coherence through collective song. We will have opening acts with Madhu Anziani and AeaLuz, each bringing their own unique expression of devotional music and heartfelt artistry.

The journey then continues with Jens Jarvie, offering songs born through years of ceremony, prayer, and deep listening. Accompanied by his band, Jens invites the audience into an uplifting experience of liberation songs and soulful storytelling, creating a bridge that leads us beautifully into the night's headlining performance.

The evening culminates with the headlining act, Curawaka, whose music has touched hearts around the world through its joyful celebration of life, indigenous wisdom, and our sacred relationship with the living Earth.

This is more than a concert, it is a woven prayer for the healing and wellbeing of all life everywhere. It is an invitation to gather and come together in community, to sing, dance, listen, celebrate, and remember what it feels like to be fully alive.

Together we'll create an evening of beauty, connection, and inspiration that feeds the soil of our lives and  helps us to walk in a good way remembering our relationship to the great mystery and all that lives and breathes through us as the infinite expression of consciousness into being. 

We look forward to welcoming you!!

title: Haunted Wine Tour & Tasting
location: Buena Vista Historical Winery
description:
This fall, Buena Vista Winery invites you to uncover the mysteries, legends, and ghostly encounters woven into more than 165 years of history. Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.

title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Newcomer Meeting in Santa Rosa

description:
**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits.

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on **Sundays from 4:00 – 5:00 PM** **at Christ Church United Methodist, 1717 Yulupa Ave., Room #4, Santa Rosa**. Contact: Abigail (707) 293-5888. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html .

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan.

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

**Visit:** https://www.northbayoa.org/

**Find a meeting:** https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

title: John Prine Tribute with David Luning, Jason Crosby, Ben Dubin and Victoria George
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental
description:
David Luning, who attended Harmony School (now OCA) returns to our stage for a special tribute celebrating John Prine's birthday. David will be joined by impressive musical colleagues Jason Crosby, Ben Dubin and Victoria George.
Tickets are $35, $30 for OCA members.
Get Tickets
This show will take place in our auditorium. Doors open at 5:30 PM.
David Luning knew at a young age the path his life should take. Throughout generations, troubadours and singers have harnessed the cultural landscape and passed it along, with the likes of John Prine and Townes Van Zandt paving the way with the telling of their stories. Following in those footsteps, the Sonoma County singer/songwriter's new record is the product of a massive turn in his life and taps into that cultural archive. Listening to ‘Souvenirs’ by John Prine, was a cornerstone moment, compelling Luning to leave Berklee College and follow in the tradition of these iconic troubadours.
Learn more about David Luning.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
location: 1st Street Gallery @ WTRSHD
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

title: California Native Creations Art Show

description:
September is the 17th Annual Pomo Honoring Month. On Monday, Sept. 14, the 6th California Native Creations Art Show opens Person Senior Wing, Finley Community Center, 2060 W. College Ave., Santa Rosa, CA. The show is free and open to the public Monday – Friday, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m., through November 19.

The established and up-and-coming native artists create with digital media, paint and traditional materials in their art, weaving, regalia, beadwork, jewelry, baskets and quilts. The artists include:

·         Meyo Marrufo, painter, guest curator for the de Young Museum and the Sonoma Valley Art Museum,

·         Buffie Campbell, Vice Chair, Sherwood Valley Rancheria, cultural teacher and master basket maker,

·         Henry Edward Frank, Yurok/Kashaya Pomo, who will show paintings and work with Legos titled Mind Prison,

·         Digital artist Nicolas \(Nico\) Vargas, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians, whose art was featured at the 55th Annual Stanford Powwow.

·         plus Gloria Carretero; Rose Hammock; Rudy Hammock; Jocelyn Garcia; Arella Ortega LaRose, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Angelica Smith, Manchester Point Arena and Yokayo Rancheria; Maria Pasalo; Michelle Napoli; Martina Morgan, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Hands Lopez; Shashoni Hanover-Redenbaugh; Katie Williams-Elliott, Juan Partida, and Mia Pasalo, Big Valley Pomo Tribe.

description:
Nataraja School of Traditional Yoga
All Classes RSVP Only at least 24hrs prior
[[breathprayeryoga@protonmail.com](mailto:breathprayeryoga@protonmail.com)]([mailto:breathprayeryoga@protonmail.com](http://mailto:breathprayeryoga@protonmail.com/)), 707-235-1413
\**For All Classes - Certain injuries & health issues may be contraindicated - Please contact me if you have a concern*
**Talasana Krama (Foundational Sequence) & Pranayama**
**Mondays 9-10:30am - Songbird Cotati - RSVP**
**$25, Discounted Class Passes & Sliding Scale Available**
Fundamental practices for understanding the holistic nature, energetics and Sanskrit yoga philosophy guiding the approach of this comprehensive system. Long time yoga practitioners as well as new students will benefit. Experience the distinction of this system verses other modern yoga/vinyasa practices commonly taught & the traditional & precise use of ujjayi breath as it relates to the Sanskrit parameters, moving with the breath and the importance of the pause. Talasana is a very unique & profound krama initiating & establishing "samasthiti", the steadiness and focus of mind, balanced energy and steadiness of body - with the two feet together, moving from the center, all the major joints and muscles of the body are exercised using arm and hand movements, back bends, side bends, twists, forward bends, squats and balancing foot stretches. The fingers interlaced create a prana circuit as they come together in the repetitive movement over the head. The breath specific movements stretch the diaphragm, psoas, massage the heart and internal organs, clear the lungs, drain the lymphatic system, stimulate the vagus nerve and calm the mind. Energy is created along the spine and central nervous system, and is distributed throughout the nadis and into the entire energy body. Regular practice of Talasana flowers into to ananta samapatti and understanding "stillness in movement".
Class begins with Opening Mantras & Ding Namaskar (Devotional Salutation to the Directional Spheres with Breath & Mantra). Then moves to Tāĺāsana to Savasana then Seated Prānāyāma (Yogic Breathing) including Morning Cleansing Kriyas, Ujjayi, Nadi Shuddi, Samantraka Prānāyāma, Pratyahara, Dharana. May include Specific Mudra (Energetic Bodily Gestures).

title: Blessing of the Acorn
location: Galbreath Wildlands Preserve
description: In collaboration with Anderson Valley Land Trust, join us to harvest tanoak acorns, learn about their value, traditions around them, and how to select the best acorns, care for them, and prepare them for eating. Acorns are a traditional food source for indigenous people throughout the United States. Historically, they have provided up to 40 percent of sustenance for Pomo people, and serve as a rich source of protein and fats. In the North Bay, the most highly prized acorn comes from the tanoak tree, or chishkale, the Pomo word for tanoak. This member of the beech family is not a true oak, but a cousin whose acorn comes adorned with a furry showy hat said to be the envy of the other oaks with their flat or vaguely bumpy caps.

title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two ofrendas in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.

Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures.  An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.

The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

The Community Ofrenda will be a shared, participatory offering. Visitors, locals, volunteers, Board members, and employees can contribute a small photograph, written name, memory, drawing or message honoring someone who has passed away – including a beloved pet. 

The installation will grow throughout October as more people participate.  Materials will be available at the display for visitors who would like to join the celebration and contribute a name, memory or even a drawing of their loved one.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.

description:
Ready to take your salsa to the next level? Salsa lessons in Marin will help you to add some flair and fluidity to your salsa dancing.

Pre-requisite: Salsa Beginners 1 – You know your basic steps, left turn, right turn, cross-body lead, and you hold your frame.

What You’ll Learn

We’ve curated a curriculum designed to build your confidence and your “social dance” vocabulary:

• The Cross Body Lead \(CBL\) Series: Master both Inside and Outside Turns, the essential building blocks for moving your partner across the floor with grace.

• The “I Turn – You Turn”: A classic social dance staple that develops timing and hand-change coordination.

• The Walk-Through: Learn how to transition smoothly through the dance space without breaking your rhythm.

• Footwork & Shine: We’ll break down the footwork pattern that adds personality to your “shines.”

Technique & Artistry

• Dancing is about more than just where your feet go. In this level, we dive deeper into the “how”:

• The Frame: Understand the “tension and compression” needed to lead and follow clearly without using muscle.

• Upper Body Mechanics: Learn how to isolate your ribcage and shoulders to move with that authentic Latin soul.

• Connection: Developing a “heavy” but responsive arm connection to ensure your partner feels every lead.

Important Details

• No dance experience required: Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

• No partner necessary: Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

• Please wear non-marking shoe soles: This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
location: 1st Street Gallery @ WTRSHD
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two ofrendas in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.

Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures.  An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.

The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

The Community Ofrenda will be a shared, participatory offering. Visitors, locals, volunteers, Board members, and employees can contribute a small photograph, written name, memory, drawing or message honoring someone who has passed away – including a beloved pet. 

The installation will grow throughout October as more people participate.  Materials will be available at the display for visitors who would like to join the celebration and contribute a name, memory or even a drawing of their loved one.

This class focuses on the simple delight of mixing color with water, brushing it on paper, and watching what happens as it moves and dries. You will learn easy ways to create paintings that are all about color and the sometimes unpredictable nature of water.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    **www.upstairsart gallery.net** 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

Readers Theatre participants read scripts adapted from literature, while the ‘audience’ pictures the action by hearing the script being read aloud. It requires no sets, costumes, props, or memorized lines. Salsa Class Beginners

Turns and Spins:

Master your inside and outside turns, double spins, and the elegant 360 and Hand Toss moves.

Intricate Patterns:

location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental, CA 95465
description:
Rest & Renew at our Sound Bath!
Support your nervous system, release anxiety and stress, and harmonize your body, mind and spirit on the 2nd Tuesday of every month! Laura Benson has a Masters in Intuition Medicine(R) and is a certified sound healer who will guide you through a gentle meditation before each sound bath session. Bring your own yoga mat & blanket and come ready to rest and renew! In the OCA Studio.
Sliding scale pricing $25-$35.
Register
A sound bath is a whole-body, immersive listening experience. During a sound bath, participants often sit or lie down, and are surrounded by the mostly non-melodic soundscapes created by a range of instruments played by the sound bath facilitator. Hence, they are “bathed” in sound.
Sound therapy is a non-invasive healing modality that utilizes the physical and physiological interactions of sound on our bodies and nervous systems to produce therapeutic results. In a sound healing session, specific sonic frequencies are used to soothe the central nervous system, calm the breath, and quiet the mind by encouraging the brain to move into more relaxed states, down from beta (fight-or-flight) and into theta and alpha waves. This increases present-moment awareness and reduces stress and anxiety. Sound baths have been found to be effective in improving mood, cognitive function, and overall mental, physical, and spiritual wellbeing.
Crystal bowl sound baths are particularly powerful in that each bowl is tuned to a specific frequency that corresponds with a different chakra, or energy center, of the body. Based on specific needs, a practitioner can focus on releasing tension or clearing out stuck energy in specific chakras by playing certain bowls or intervals.
While attending a sound bath, you may experience physical sensations brought out by the crystal sound bowls or gong, such as tingling in your limbs or scalp, slowing of your breathing, eye flutters, or small muscle spasms. Not to worry! These sensations often indicate the release of tension or emotional energy stored in the body’s energy systems.

title: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market
location: Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
description: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a year-round Saturday tradition in Sonoma County, bringing together local farmers, ranchers, food artisans, and neighbors from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. This is not just a place to shop, it's a place to connect directly with the people who grow your food. As a Slow Food Sonoma County award recipient, the market prioritizes integrity, seasonality, and true farm-to-community relationships. Expect peak-season produce harvested just hours before market, pasture-raised meats, fresh flowers, artisan breads, handcrafted goods, and thoughtfully prepared foods that reflect the region's agricultural richness. Visitors can stroll the vibrant open-air market, sample local flavors, and experience Sonoma County's food culture in its most authentic form. Families, chefs, and weekend explorers alike gather here to discover what's growing now and to support small farms that keep our local food system strong. Open every Saturday, rain or shine, the Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a cornerstone of the community and a must-visit stop for anyone wanting to taste, shop, and experience Sonoma County at its freshest.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
location: 1st Street Gallery @ WTRSHD
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

September is the 17th Annual Pomo Honoring Month. On Monday, Sept. 14, the 6th California Native Creations Art Show opens Person Senior Wing, Finley Community Center, 2060 W. College Ave., Santa Rosa, CA. The show is free and open to the public Monday – Friday, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m., through November 19.

The established and up-and-coming native artists create with digital media, paint and traditional materials in their art, weaving, regalia, beadwork, jewelry, baskets and quilts. The artists include:

·         Meyo Marrufo, painter, guest curator for the de Young Museum and the Sonoma Valley Art Museum,

·         Buffie Campbell, Vice Chair, Sherwood Valley Rancheria, cultural teacher and master basket maker,

·         Henry Edward Frank, Yurok/Kashaya Pomo, who will show paintings and work with Legos titled Mind Prison,

·         Digital artist Nicolas \(Nico\) Vargas, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians, whose art was featured at the 55th Annual Stanford Powwow.

·         plus Gloria Carretero; Rose Hammock; Rudy Hammock; Jocelyn Garcia; Arella Ortega LaRose, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Angelica Smith, Manchester Point Arena and Yokayo Rancheria; Maria Pasalo; Michelle Napoli; Martina Morgan, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Hands Lopez; Shashoni Hanover-Redenbaugh; Katie Williams-Elliott, Juan Partida, and Mia Pasalo, Big Valley Pomo Tribe.

title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two ofrendas in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.

Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures.  An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.

The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

The Community Ofrenda will be a shared, participatory offering. Visitors, locals, volunteers, Board members, and employees can contribute a small photograph, written name, memory, drawing or message honoring someone who has passed away – including a beloved pet. 

The installation will grow throughout October as more people participate.  Materials will be available at the display for visitors who would like to join the celebration and contribute a name, memory or even a drawing of their loved one.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
location: Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    **www.upstairsart gallery.net** 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: Rainbow Book Club: Bury Your Gays by Chuck Tingle
description: The Rainbow Book Club is cohosted by Mindy from Napa County Library and Napa Bookmine staff members Kass and Jules. The book club focuses on books that explore and embrace queer identity. This is a free event, but we appreciate your RSVP so we can plan for your attendance! We look forward to welcoming you. ABOUT THE BOOK "Brilliantly bloody, wildly fun, and extremely scary, Bury Your Gays brings a sledgehammer down on tired tropes and makes a masterpiece of their guts." — Rachel Harrison, national bestselling author of Black Sheep “Brilliantly bloody, wildly fun, and extremely scary, Bury Your Gays brings a sledgehammer down on tired tropes and makes a masterpiece of their guts. A profoundly smart and emotionally resonant novel that is sprinkled with cinema magic and a brutal Hollywood reckoning.” — Rachel Harrison, national bestselling author of So Thirsty "This triumph of a book effortlessly and cleverly upends clichés. One of the best novels ever about LA, the film industry, and horror movies, it delivers all the fandom, fear, and feels, and then some. Only Chuck Tingle can tell a story as masterfully as this, and he once again proves that love is so real." — CJ Leede, author of American Rapture The instant USA Today bestseller by Chuck Tingle about what it takes to succeed in a world that wants you dead. Named one of the Best Horror Books of 2024 \(Esquire, Parade, and Library Journal\) • Winner of the Locus Award for Best Horror Novel • A Lambda Literary Award finalist! • Winner of the 2025 Locus Award for Best Horror Novel • A Best Horror Book of 2024 \(Esquire\) • One of the Best Books of Summer 2024 \(Esquire, Paste, HuffPost, Publishers Weekly\) • Winner of the 2025 Libby Award for Best Horror • Winner of the 2025 RUSA Horror Reading List • Winner of the 2025 Dragon Award for Best Horror Novel • A CALIBA Golden Poppy Award finalist • A GoodReads Choice Award finalist for Best Horror • An Indie Next and LibraryReads Pick Misha knows that chasing success in Hollywood can be hell. But finally, after years of trying to make it, his big moment is here: an Oscar nomination. And the executives at the studio for his long-running streaming series know just the thing to kick his career to the next level: kill off the gay characters, "for the algorithm," in the upcoming season finale. Misha refuses, but he soon realizes that he’s just put a target on his back. And what’s worse, monsters from his horror movie days are stalking him and his friends through the hills above Los Angeles. Haunted by his past, Misha must risk his entire future—before the horrors from the silver screen find a way to bury him for good. ABOUT THE AUTHOR CHUCK TINGLE is the USA Today bestselling author of Camp Damascus, Bury Your Gays, and Straight. His books have been finalists for the Bram Stoker and CALIBA Golden Poppy Award. He is a mysterious force of energy behind sunglasses and a pink mask. He is also an anonymous author of romance, horror, and fantasy. Tingle was born in Home of Truth, Utah and now lives in Los Angeles, California. Tingle writes to prove love is real, because love is the most important tool we have when resisting the endless cosmic void. Not everything people say about Tingle is true, but the important parts are.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
location: 1st Street Gallery @ WTRSHD
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

description:
