title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
location: 1st Street Gallery @ WTRSHD
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

title: California Native Creations Art Show
location: Person Senior Wing, Finley Community Center
description:
September is the 17th Annual Pomo Honoring Month. On Monday, Sept. 14, the 6th California Native Creations Art Show opens Person Senior Wing, Finley Community Center, 2060 W. College Ave., Santa Rosa, CA. The show is free and open to the public Monday – Friday, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m., through November 19.

The established and up-and-coming native artists create with digital media, paint and traditional materials in their art, weaving, regalia, beadwork, jewelry, baskets and quilts. The artists include:

·         Meyo Marrufo, painter, guest curator for the de Young Museum and the Sonoma Valley Art Museum,

·         Buffie Campbell, Vice Chair, Sherwood Valley Rancheria, cultural teacher and master basket maker,

·         Henry Edward Frank, Yurok/Kashaya Pomo, who will show paintings and work with Legos titled Mind Prison,

·         Digital artist Nicolas \(Nico\) Vargas, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians, whose art was featured at the 55th Annual Stanford Powwow.

·         plus Gloria Carretero; Rose Hammock; Rudy Hammock; Jocelyn Garcia; Arella Ortega LaRose, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Angelica Smith, Manchester Point Arena and Yokayo Rancheria; Maria Pasalo; Michelle Napoli; Martina Morgan, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Hands Lopez; Shashoni Hanover-Redenbaugh; Katie Williams-Elliott, Juan Partida, and Mia Pasalo, Big Valley Pomo Tribe.

**Talasana Krama (Foundational Sequence) & Pranayama**

**$25, Discounted Class Passes & Sliding Scale Available**
Fundamental practices for understanding the holistic nature, energetics and Sanskrit yoga philosophy guiding the approach of this comprehensive system. Long time yoga practitioners as well as new students will benefit. Experience the distinction of this system verses other modern yoga/vinyasa practices commonly taught & the traditional & precise use of ujjayi breath as it relates to the Sanskrit parameters, moving with the breath and the importance of the pause. Talasana is a very unique & profound krama initiating & establishing "samasthiti", the steadiness and focus of mind, balanced energy and steadiness of body - with the two feet together, moving from the center, all the major joints and muscles of the body are exercised using arm and hand movements, back bends, side bends, twists, forward bends, squats and balancing foot stretches. The fingers interlaced create a prana circuit as they come together in the repetitive movement over the head. The breath specific movements stretch the diaphragm, psoas, massage the heart and internal organs, clear the lungs, drain the lymphatic system, stimulate the vagus nerve and calm the mind. Energy is created along the spine and central nervous system, and is distributed throughout the nadis and into the entire energy body. Regular practice of Talasana flowers into to ananta samapatti and understanding "stillness in movement".
Class begins with Opening Mantras & Ding Namaskar (Devotional Salutation to the Directional Spheres with Breath & Mantra). Then moves to Tāĺāsana to Savasana then Seated Prānāyāma (Yogic Breathing) including Morning Cleansing Kriyas, Ujjayi, Nadi Shuddi, Samantraka Prānāyāma, Pratyahara, Dharana. May include Specific Mudra (Energetic Bodily Gestures).

title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two ofrendas in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.

Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures.  An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.

The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

The Community Ofrenda will be a shared, participatory offering. Visitors, locals, volunteers, Board members, and employees can contribute a small photograph, written name, memory, drawing or message honoring someone who has passed away – including a beloved pet. 

The installation will grow throughout October as more people participate.  Materials will be available at the display for visitors who would like to join the celebration and contribute a name, memory or even a drawing of their loved one.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: Haunted Wine Tour & Tasting

description:
This fall, Buena Vista Winery invites you to uncover the mysteries, legends, and ghostly encounters woven into more than 165 years of history. Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.

title: Salsa Beginners 2 - Mondays
location: Salsa Dance Marin
description:
Ready to take your salsa to the next level? Salsa lessons in Marin will help you to add some flair and fluidity to your salsa dancing.

Pre-requisite: Salsa Beginners 1 – You know your basic steps, left turn, right turn, cross-body lead, and you hold your frame.

What You’ll Learn

We’ve curated a curriculum designed to build your confidence and your “social dance” vocabulary:

• The Cross Body Lead \(CBL\) Series: Master both Inside and Outside Turns, the essential building blocks for moving your partner across the floor with grace.

• The “I Turn – You Turn”: A classic social dance staple that develops timing and hand-change coordination.

• The Walk-Through: Learn how to transition smoothly through the dance space without breaking your rhythm.

• Footwork & Shine: We’ll break down the footwork pattern that adds personality to your “shines.”

Technique & Artistry

• Dancing is about more than just where your feet go. In this level, we dive deeper into the “how”:

• The Frame: Understand the “tension and compression” needed to lead and follow clearly without using muscle.

• Upper Body Mechanics: Learn how to isolate your ribcage and shoulders to move with that authentic Latin soul.

• Connection: Developing a “heavy” but responsive arm connection to ensure your partner feels every lead.

Important Details

• No dance experience required: Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

• No partner necessary: Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

• Please wear non-marking shoe soles: This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
location: 1st Street Gallery @ WTRSHD
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two ofrendas in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.

Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures.  An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.

The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

The Community Ofrenda will be a shared, participatory offering. Visitors, locals, volunteers, Board members, and employees can contribute a small photograph, written name, memory, drawing or message honoring someone who has passed away – including a beloved pet. 

The installation will grow throughout October as more people participate.  Materials will be available at the display for visitors who would like to join the celebration and contribute a name, memory or even a drawing of their loved one.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

location: Luther Burbank Art and Garden Center
description:
Learn about colorful and interesting dragonflies and their unique biology with field biologist Sandra von Arb, co-author of *Dragonflies (Anisoptera) of California* with Kathy Biggs. Sandra will share her knowledge of the 47 species that occur here, how to identify them, what the dragonflies need for survival, where to find them, and their migratory habits.

Sandra von Arb has been a professional wildlife biologist for 30 years, focusing on sensitive and endangered species in northern California, southern Oregon, and northern Illinois. She is a co-founder of Biodiversity Education and Research Foundation, whose mission is to foster ecological stewardship through science and education.

title: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market
location: Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
description: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a year-round Saturday tradition in Sonoma County, bringing together local farmers, ranchers, food artisans, and neighbors from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. This is not just a place to shop, it's a place to connect directly with the people who grow your food. As a Slow Food Sonoma County award recipient, the market prioritizes integrity, seasonality, and true farm-to-community relationships. Expect peak-season produce harvested just hours before market, pasture-raised meats, fresh flowers, artisan breads, handcrafted goods, and thoughtfully prepared foods that reflect the region's agricultural richness. Visitors can stroll the vibrant open-air market, sample local flavors, and experience Sonoma County's food culture in its most authentic form. Families, chefs, and weekend explorers alike gather here to discover what's growing now and to support small farms that keep our local food system strong. Open every Saturday, rain or shine, the Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a cornerstone of the community and a must-visit stop for anyone wanting to taste, shop, and experience Sonoma County at its freshest.

Upcycled Journal WorkshopWednesday, October 21st, 6:00-9:00pmAges 13+ Attendance $60 + Materials $10 = $70.00 Registration Fee Join us for a fun and creative workshop turning recycled cereal/snack boxes into a unique handmade journal. Students will remove parts of the boxes until we have what we will use as our cover.  Then, using miscellaneous papers, we fold these into the pages of our journals. With simple book-binding skills using a needle and waxed thread, we will stitch the pages into our covers. We will also decorate the covers of our journals with collage papers and/or paint. Examples will be shown throughout the class, and step-by-step instruction with all materials being provided, this class is great for beginners looking to get started in upcycled crafting. Short exercises to boost your creativity and journal prompts are also included. Whether you are a beginning or seasoned artist/writer/crafter, or just looking to try something new, this is a great way to get inspired and create something meaningful to you. About the Instructor: Rendell Hourigan received a BBA in Marketing from Texas Tech University, and has pursued art for over 25 years focusing on sustainable mixed media. She has studied with artists including Chery Baird, Jenny London, and Teri Slot, exploring drawing, collage, and soft pastels. She’s exhibited work at the Sebastopol Center for the Arts, The Graton Gallery, and her SOFA district studio. Drawn to the beauty of discarded materials and passionate about recycling, she incorporates reclaimed materials into her work and now leads art workshops to inspire eco-conscious creativity in others.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
location: 1st Street Gallery @ WTRSHD
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two ofrendas in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.

Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures.  An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.

The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

The Community Ofrenda will be a shared, participatory offering. Visitors, locals, volunteers, Board members, and employees can contribute a small photograph, written name, memory, drawing or message honoring someone who has passed away – including a beloved pet. 

The installation will grow throughout October as more people participate.  Materials will be available at the display for visitors who would like to join the celebration and contribute a name, memory or even a drawing of their loved one.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
location: Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    **www.upstairsart gallery.net** 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: Give 'Em the Axe! Ladies Night at the Range in Santa Rosa
description:
Sonoma County Women's Wine Club (SCWWC)
Join us for an axe-throwing session to blow off some steam. I'm super excited to be able to offer a ladies' Axe-throwing night in Santa Rosa. If you've ever had a curiosity about this fun activity, this is your chance to find out more!

We have reserved a group spot with the indoor range on a Wednesday night. It will consist of an introductory lesson, and then we all get to practice taking turns. Everyone will get ample time to practice, as they have many lanes.

This event is focused on a less-competitive, relaxed, and entertaining atmosphere. All skill levels are encouraged. All equipment and targets are provided by them, and we will probably get about 1 to 2 hours to enjoy ourselves.

I encourage everyone to bring a bottle of wine or a snack to share with the rest of the group (We usually end up with a lovely charcuterie and wine spread for everyone to enjoy).

There are 10 spots available, guests welcome. The ladies' group lesson and event is $31 per person, with $6 prepaid via Paypal and $25 paid to the range.

Please only RSVP 'Yes' if you are able to make it, hostess Daima Phipps will be collecting a $6 fee via Paypal to hold your spot. Paypal/Meetup should lead you to make your payment after you RSVP 'Yes'.

Closed-toed shoes are recommended.

There is an attendance policy for all our events: if you No-Show to three events, you may not attend events for the next three months. Please put this event in your calendar so you don't miss out or get dinged. A No-Show is when you are on the 'Going' list, but do not show up.

Cheers, and hope to see you there!

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
location: 1st Street Gallery @ WTRSHD
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

title: California Native Creations Art Show
location: Person Senior Wing, Finley Community Center
description:
September is the 17th Annual Pomo Honoring Month. On Monday, Sept. 14, the 6th California Native Creations Art Show opens Person Senior Wing, Finley Community Center, 2060 W. College Ave., Santa Rosa, CA. The show is free and open to the public Monday – Friday, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m., through November 19.

The established and up-and-coming native artists create with digital media, paint and traditional materials in their art, weaving, regalia, beadwork, jewelry, baskets and quilts. The artists include:

·         Meyo Marrufo, painter, guest curator for the de Young Museum and the Sonoma Valley Art Museum,

·         Buffie Campbell, Vice Chair, Sherwood Valley Rancheria, cultural teacher and master basket maker,

·         Henry Edward Frank, Yurok/Kashaya Pomo, who will show paintings and work with Legos titled Mind Prison,

·         Digital artist Nicolas \(Nico\) Vargas, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians, whose art was featured at the 55th Annual Stanford Powwow.

·         plus Gloria Carretero; Rose Hammock; Rudy Hammock; Jocelyn Garcia; Arella Ortega LaRose, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Angelica Smith, Manchester Point Arena and Yokayo Rancheria; Maria Pasalo; Michelle Napoli; Martina Morgan, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Hands Lopez; Shashoni Hanover-Redenbaugh; Katie Williams-Elliott, Juan Partida, and Mia Pasalo, Big Valley Pomo Tribe.

description:
Nataraja School of Traditional Yoga
**Yoga Vinyasa Krama - Thursdays 9-10:30am**
**Songbird Community Healing Center Cotati**
**RSVP ONLY**
Physical Health, Conditioning, Pranic Flow, Vital Energy, Mental Focus & Stillness - through intelligent architecture with the metaphysics of deep conscious breathing & slow motion, yogic breathwork, mantra/sound/vibration, mudra, subtle & contemplative practices.
Yoga Vinyasa Krama is a comprehensive hatha-raja yogic system for purification, developing concentration, neuromuscular fitness and conditioning, refining & mastering the breath, awakening subtle energy and stilling the mind. Based on deep breathing & the subtle movement of prana directed into the cartilage tissue, sinuous musculature, internal organs, nerve pathways and nadis. It has over 700 intelligently sequenced slow, conscious breath powered with precision movement variations with pause (vinyasas), exploring many aesthetic variations of each posture to correctly establish the main asanas while the mind merges with the breath.
Includes the energetics of drishti, pratikriyas, bandha, vaseth, mudra, mantra, surya & ding namaskar with breath & mantra, cleansing kriyas, Himalayan pranayama including including ujjayi variations, heating & cooling breaths, solar, lunar & soli-lunar nadi shuddhi practices, pranava & samantraka pranayama, pratyahara, subtle & contemplative practices in 12 kramas (sequences).
The whole process gradually transforms the body and mind, releasing old patterns of physical and mental tension and dysfunctional patterns of movement, providing tonic, energetic and psychophysiological effects.
This system is presented from the teachings **Srivatsa Ramaswami** learned through his over 33 years of one on one study with **Sri Krishnamacharya** and teachings from a similar **Himalayan method**.
This ongoing class will explore the entire system of 12 Kramas with each class focusing on a particular krama or vinyasas from different kramas & pranayama & dharana practices.
Please practice on an empty stomach. Morning beverage ok but please take it 30min or more before class.

Knowledge of Ujjayi Breathing recommended

title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two ofrendas in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.

Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures.  An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.

The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

The Community Ofrenda will be a shared, participatory offering. Visitors, locals, volunteers, Board members, and employees can contribute a small photograph, written name, memory, drawing or message honoring someone who has passed away – including a beloved pet. 

The installation will grow throughout October as more people participate.  Materials will be available at the display for visitors who would like to join the celebration and contribute a name, memory or even a drawing of their loved one.

From the first signs of autumn in October to the brilliant display of rare Asian maples in November and the quiet beauty of early winter in December, each visit offers something new to discover. 

Maple Magic & Winter Wonder invites visitors to experience this special time of year through nature, creativity, and connection. title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
location: Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: S.R. Laws
location: Café Frida Gallery
description:
S.R. LAWS IS OUT THERE: He approaches songwriting with a passion for songs that we all grew up on. His sound rings a familiar bell in your head while still delivering ideas completely unique.  He draws inspiration from outstanding storytellers like John Hiatt, Lou Reed, Steve Earle, Neil Finn and Ron Sexsmith. All of their music and others have carved a deep groove. 

Growing up out there in Northern California, he developed a unique connection to music early on. His father worked as a trash collector, and he would spend hours sifting through bags of discarded 45 records. Each find felt like stumbling upon hidden treasures. Some records were covered in dirt and grime, while others were pristine. The thrill of discovering new sounds was exhilarating, and he could hardly wait to drop the needle and immerse himself in the music.

He embarked on a pilgrimage to Texas with just two suitcases and $500 in his bank account. His goal was to dive into the vibrant music scene and learn from fellow songwriters. Austin, known as the "Live Music Capital of the World," offered countless opportunities for him to grow as an artist. Open mics and songwriters' nights became his training ground, where he soaked up every moment, listening to others share their stories through music.

These days, he resides in Sonoma County, California, working hard as a touring artist and singer-songwriter for his original rock band, The Heartsleeves. He invites everyone to join him on this musical journey, sharing his songs one person at a time in this vast and unpredictable world we live in.

“Scott Ray Laws is an unique and really cool songwriter…he digs into materials, tells a story in his songs, and has a clean baritone vocality that is easy on the ears. We had a chance to meet and hang with Scott back in May ..and I HAD to have him back for a Wednesday evening.” Luigi- Owner-The Listening Room.

“..An ORIGINAL songwriter who knows how to tell a story clearly in song” -  Scotty O’Neill - Guitarist/Promoter

“ It was such a treat catching your set last night — really refreshing to hear something new and original. Thanks for pulling up a chair and hanging out with us — we really enjoyed the conversation and the stories behind your songs.”  -Tripp B. - Sonoma Songwriter

“Expect slow burning passion and vivid music …the kind of energy that turns into “let’s stay for just one more!..”  - Doug- Owner/Wine Maker- Spicy Vines

“...His lyrics simply tell first-person stories from his own life. Nothing fancy, he's not writing to impress--he pours himself, as is, into each phrase and melody.”- Rebecca Roudman- Dirty Cello Radio Hour KRCB Radio 104.9 FM

“ It is through forthright lyrics that are personal and earnest, that he composes lyrical pictures. Taking snapshots from the most common walks of life...”  - David Sampson - Producer Studio Secti West

“..relaxed mid-tempo Americana, capturing in each song the rhythmic pocket Laws is known for creating.” -  Coyote Music Review 2024

Oil painting doesn’t have to be intimidating! In just four weeks, students will paint a portrait in the indirect style, starting with a grey value study, building up with layers, and finishing with powerful details. The final result always surprises people: just by following basic rules, anyone can create a beautiful oil portrait that glows. Even abstract painters can benefit from learning these techniques.

Knowing how oil painting works gives us more confidence to develop our own authentic creative voice. As Maggie says, “You gotta learn the rules to break the rules.”

Maggie Parr started her career working as a show designer at Walt Disney Imagineering, where she designed theme park attractions around the world. She also expanded into book illustration, murals, portraits, comics, and eventually, writing books and scripts for television. She also developed her own painting practice. To that end, she studied with master teachers like Steve Huston, Jeremy Lipking, and Joseph Q. Daily. She got an MFA and taught at the college level, then developed her own teaching methods for private and group study. Today, Maggie maintains a thriving business creating custom art and designs for corporations, individuals, and non-profits.

She teaches other artists to utilize classical rendering techniques so they can confidently break the rules in the service of their own work. And she coaches creatives in search of deeper authenticity, healing, and self-actualization.

title: Django Festival Allstars
location: The Raven Performing Arts Theater
description:
Django’s unmistakable cool and jumpin’ joie de vivre have made him an icon for an unlikely range of luminaries from Carlos Santana to Eric Clapton, guitar greats! Jimi Hendrix named his “big band of gypsies” in tribute,  and Willie Nelson adopted his influence in “country-swing.”

The Django Festival Allstars have grown into a brilliantly cohesive group of star musicians who’ve taken America by storm, performing at top concert halls and festivals to standing ovations. They’ve appeared at SFJazz, Kennedy Center, Dizzy’s and Rose Hall, Jazz@Lincoln Center, Keystone Korner, Hollywood Bowl, Montreal Jazz Festival and Arts Centers, Kimmel, Strathmore, and many more, including Carnegie Hall and Birdland (for 25 years). 

The music speaks of Paris in the 20s and 30s when “gitane” music filled the air, in the cafés, the streets, in the countryside, a romantic Paris with lovers, campfires, a time of Montmartre, la belle époque, le Boudon café, café au lait, luscious pastry, and a great glass of wine. Django was “king’.”  He teamed with Jazz Violinist Stephane Grappelli and made musical history.

The Django Festival Allstars bring this music to today… combining known standards and original music…intoxicating!! They swing like crazy and will break your heart with a ballad. Their special guests have been Randy Brecker, Joe Lovano, Regina Carter, Cyrille Aimee, Ken Peplowski, Madeleine Peyroux, Sefon Harris, James Carter, to name a few. 

**Saturday, November 22nd, 7PM.**

title: Gain Speaking Confidence with Mare Island Toastmasters
description:

Usually at our meetings, we will have a prepared speech, and a speech evaluation. The Grammarian and Wizard of Ah's will listen for turns of phrases and the use of filler words. We also practice impromptu speaking during the section of the meeting called Table Topics. During Table Topics, at a recent meeting, we were asked what we felt was the biggest communication problem or challenge. What would you answer in a fast moment? Table topics will challenge you to think quickly and give an answer without preparation.

You will also hear tips on public speaking skills at our upcoming meeting. Whether you're a seasoned traveler or just looking for some adventure from the comfort of your home, this event is perfect for you.

title: Analog Dog
location: HopMonk Tavern
description:
Analog Dog makes genre fluid music in San Francisco, USA. Hailing from all corners of the country, the band came together in and around the hallowed musical breeding grounds of Golden Gate Park, with the intent to carry on the spirit of the legendary musical city. With each member drawing on diverse inspirations and musical backgrounds, from self-taught to classically trained, they unite over a common love for genre-bending composition and improvisation. Honoring the vibrations of the psychedelic revolution of the 1960s, digging into the disco grooves from the dance revolution of the 1970s, and simultaneously embracing modern indie pop soundscapes, Analog Dog is its own thing.

The release of their multi-genre debut LP 'Color TV' was a landmark success for the band last year, and the same can be expected with the release of their 2nd full length LP 'IT'S NOT THE MONEY WE'LL REMEMBER'. With recent performances including opening for The Script at the famed Fox Theater in Oakland, a two week tour to Mexico City, summer tour dates throughout the western U.S., and having thrown their own festivals for thousands of music fans in Golden Gate Park and Jerry Garcia Amphitheater over the last few years, the band has willed their way into the hearts of Bay Area and international audiences alike. As they set their sights on the next step, Analog Dog is committed to creating a vibration that reminds every audience of the magic that exists within all of us.

San Francisco based band Analog Dog announced that their new record IT’S NOT THE MONEY WE’LL REMEMBER will be released January 16, 2026. The album comes after the release of six psychedelic disco fusion singles which have received love from around the world. As they prepare for their headline tour in support of the record, the band is continuing to demonstrate that they have something truly unique, fresh and deep to offer people.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
location: 1st Street Gallery @ WTRSHD
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

The established and up-and-coming native artists create with digital media, paint and traditional materials in their art, weaving, regalia, beadwork, jewelry, baskets and quilts. The artists include:

·         Meyo Marrufo, painter, guest curator for the de Young Museum and the Sonoma Valley Art Museum,

·         Buffie Campbell, Vice Chair, Sherwood Valley Rancheria, cultural teacher and master basket maker,

·         Henry Edward Frank, Yurok/Kashaya Pomo, who will show paintings and work with Legos titled Mind Prison,

·         Digital artist Nicolas \(Nico\) Vargas, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians, whose art was featured at the 55th Annual Stanford Powwow.

·         plus Gloria Carretero; Rose Hammock; Rudy Hammock; Jocelyn Garcia; Arella Ortega LaRose, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Angelica Smith, Manchester Point Arena and Yokayo Rancheria; Maria Pasalo; Michelle Napoli; Martina Morgan, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Hands Lopez; Shashoni Hanover-Redenbaugh; Katie Williams-Elliott, Juan Partida, and Mia Pasalo, Big Valley Pomo Tribe.

title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two ofrendas in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.

Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures.  An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.

The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

The Community Ofrenda will be a shared, participatory offering. Visitors, locals, volunteers, Board members, and employees can contribute a small photograph, written name, memory, drawing or message honoring someone who has passed away – including a beloved pet. 

The installation will grow throughout October as more people participate.  Materials will be available at the display for visitors who would like to join the celebration and contribute a name, memory or even a drawing of their loved one.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
location: Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    **www.upstairsart gallery.net** 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

Shut Up & Write!® Wine Country
**This event is hosted on the Shut Up & Write website, so please [sign up here](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2me5JeN600/id2w10OBEA00) for your writing event.**

**ABOUT THE EVENT**
Join us virtually for an hour + of writing using Zoom. Let's keep together as much as we can during these uncertain times and keep on writing. Look for the schedule online and join us.

We’ve discovered that it’s strikingly helpful to write with other writers. See if it’s true for you at 3pm on Friday afternoon. Be it a book, blog, script, essay, dissertation, resume, melody, poem or just plain work stuff, you are invited to write it with us. No one will see what you've written or give you unsolicited advice. Instead of just thinking about writing, come and get some real writing done.

1. Link available on the Shut Up and Write website..

4. If you won't be able to make it, please cancel so that the space is available to another writer.

SCHEDULE:
3:00 - quick intros.
around 3:10 - timer starts: write for 70 mins.
4:20 - (the end) wrap up

Wherever you are, we hope to see you online! Keep on writing...
Regards,
Lorraine Segal

title: Haunted Wine Tour & Tasting

description:
This fall, Buena Vista Winery invites you to uncover the mysteries, legends, and ghostly encounters woven into more than 165 years of history. Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.

Slow down and float into a quieter rhythm with SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River at The Floathouse Petaluma. Launching from downtown Petaluma, this peaceful on-the-water yoga experience feels worlds away from the bustle—set in the calm, protected turning basin where the river naturally invites you to relax.

This all-levels, 90-minute session welcomes everyone, from first-time paddle boarders and yoga newcomers to experienced practitioners. We begin with a short, gentle paddle from the docks to get comfortable on your board \(knees are always welcome\), then anchor together so tidal movement won’t interrupt your flow. Once settled, you’re free to move, stretch, rest, or simply be—guided by expert instruction and supported by the shared energy of the group. Evening sessions and morning sessions allow YOU to choose the vibe that suits you best.

All equipment is provided, including extra-stable paddleboards that are wider and longer than a yoga mat, designed to help you feel grounded and secure on the water.

Perfect for locals and Bay Area visitors alike, SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River offers a rare chance to experience downtown Petaluma from the water—peaceful, playful, and deeply restorative.

It’s YOUR river. Come out and play.

title: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market
location: Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
description: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a year-round Saturday tradition in Sonoma County, bringing together local farmers, ranchers, food artisans, and neighbors from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. This is not just a place to shop, it's a place to connect directly with the people who grow your food. As a Slow Food Sonoma County award recipient, the market prioritizes integrity, seasonality, and true farm-to-community relationships. Expect peak-season produce harvested just hours before market, pasture-raised meats, fresh flowers, artisan breads, handcrafted goods, and thoughtfully prepared foods that reflect the region's agricultural richness. Visitors can stroll the vibrant open-air market, sample local flavors, and experience Sonoma County's food culture in its most authentic form. Families, chefs, and weekend explorers alike gather here to discover what's growing now and to support small farms that keep our local food system strong. Open every Saturday, rain or shine, the Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a cornerstone of the community and a must-visit stop for anyone wanting to taste, shop, and experience Sonoma County at its freshest.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
location: 1st Street Gallery @ WTRSHD
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

description:
The program leaders will guide you on 8 weekly hikes with the challenge increasing each week. Leaders will have group discussions about gear, hydration, hiking poles, first aid and pacing, etc. The group's final hike aims for Bald Mountain, where hikers can enjoy stunning vistas.

The following is a list of possible routes specifically selected for this hiking series: 

1) Sat 9/26 — Creekside + Waterfall loop, 3.6 miles, 750 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 2) Sat 10/03 – Vista Trail loop, 3.4 miles, 830 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 3) Sat 10/10 – Hillside to Neptune table + Meadow, 4.4 miles, 970 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 4) Sat 10/17 – Goodspeed to Nattkemper bench, 3.8 miles, 1,240 ft elevation \[meet @ Goodspeed lot\] 5) Sat 10/24 – Hillside + Vista Trail loop, 3.6 miles, 1,070 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 6) Sat 10/31 – False Lake Meadow & Lake Ilsanjo loop in Trionne-Annadel SP, 6.1 miles, 670 ft elevation \[meet @ Annadel's Cobblestone Trailhead\] 7) Sat 11/07 – Fern Lake + Orchard loop in SDC/Jack London SHP, 5.5 miles, 1,460 ft elevation \[meet @ Walnut & North St inside SDC; park on Grove St\] 8) Sat 11/14 – Bald Mtn summit (w/optional Headwaters detour, 5.8 miles), 5.1 miles, 1,670 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\]

Please note these routes are subject to change based on the group and weather, as the group does hike in light rains. Wear appropriate footwear for rocky or slippery trails, and layers. Bring water, and if desired, a snack. The group will be limited to 35 participants. 

The hiking series costs $80 (plus a $10 parking fee per visit. Note that the Sugarloaf Annual Pass is $59 and valid at Sugarloaf and Jack London SHP), or free-of-cost for participants with a September 2026 or newer Park Rx from a Sonoma County Medical Provider.

**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits.

title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two ofrendas in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.

Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures.  An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.

The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

The Community Ofrenda will be a shared, participatory offering. Visitors, locals, volunteers, Board members, and employees can contribute a small photograph, written name, memory, drawing or message honoring someone who has passed away – including a beloved pet. 

The installation will grow throughout October as more people participate.  Materials will be available at the display for visitors who would like to join the celebration and contribute a name, memory or even a drawing of their loved one.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room

description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    **www.upstairsart gallery.net**

Join us for an unforgettable afternoon where fashion, wine, and philanthropy come together in the heart of Napa Valley.

Hosted at Frank Family Vineyards, this exclusive event celebrates our collaboration with Simkhai in support of Dress for Success, an organization dedicated to empowering women to achieve economic independence through career development, professional attire, and a global network of support.

The experience begins with a wine reception followed by a beautifully curated multi-course lunch by Bottega Napa Valley. As guests are seated on our Miller House Lawn, enjoy an inspiring panel conversation featuring Frank Family Founder, Leslie Frank, acclaimed fashion designer Jonathan Simkhai, and Dress for Success CEO Joanie Bily. Together, they'll discuss the power of purpose-driven partnerships, confidence, and self-expression through fashion and wine.

Guests will then enjoy an exclusive runway presentation of the Simkhai pieces, culminating in the debut of our limited-edition collaborative wine, created to celebrate craftsmanship, creativity, and giving back.

Throughout the afternoon, renowned color analyst, The Color Countess, will offer personalized color analysis sessions, helping guests discover the colors that best complement their natural features while celebrating confidence through personal style.

Every ticket purchased, along with a percentage of proceeds from featured wine and Simkhai apparel sales during the event, will directly support Dress for Success and its purpose to help women thrive in work and in life.

We invite you to experience an afternoon of exceptional wine, inspiring conversation, timeless fashion, and meaningful impact.

title: What We Can Know by Ian McEwan [OPTION 1]
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
***What We Can Know* by Ian McEwan**

**Ed's description**: "It is 2119, and Thomas Metcalfe is a humanities academic expert on the 90 30 era - 1990 to 2030 - when the Derangement accelerated leading eventually to the Inundation which destroyed much of the civilized world with ephemeral archives preserved in mountainous libraries while Nigeria houses ALL digital records. Thomas embarks on a hero's journey to find the long lost but legendary 'Corona for Vivien' recited by the famed poet Francis Blundy for his wife's fiftieth birthday party at an 'immortal night' with literary luminaries in 2014. In this period the STEM colleges have all the best students and facilities while Humanities colleges have the lousiest students and facilities, and Thomas hopes his finding of the corona - a poetic structure usually of seven sonnets but 15 in this case - will spark some life in his dying field. He finds Vivien's memoirs, and the second part of the novel belongs to her."

**Lucinda**: "This book was a mind bender. I never quite knew what was going on until the very end. I believe that’s the whole point. I appreciated McEwan’s views on climate decline and what it might lead to. It was thought provoking (no spoilers). I also found the book a little hard to read as it was quite detailed, and the characters might be considered amoral. There is a lot here."

**Dave**: "Intriguing novel. Pondering the future not about technological change but what will do with the vast amount of saved data. How will we encounter our history and the place for humanities in the future."

**Nancy R**: "I've started on my second reading. There's so much in the book to discuss. One thing is 100 years in the future calling global warming 'the derangement.' brilliant, among others. The story is involving and well written, and is sure to generate lively discussions."

*•* "Sophisticated entertainment of a high order." —*The New York Times*
*• "*Brilliantly, and surprisingly, plotted."—*The Washington Post •* "A novelist of consummate skill."—*The Wall Street Journal*
*•* "Elegantly structured and provocative."—*Los Angeles Times*

title: Documentary:  JAMES McNEIL WHISTLER
location: Jarvis Conservatory
description:
Whistler was a loud and fascinating character who lived life to the full. But above all, and despite all the legal scandals and verbal posturing, he was a magnificent painter, printmaker and writer. An extremely proficient and imaginative artist with a gift for creativity and expression that embraced the cult of beauty, pushed the boundaries of painting and gave birth to modern art. 

Tate Britain is now holding the first major retrospective of Whistler in three decades. This blockbuster exhibition promises to reawaken the world to just how important Whistler is to art history, uniting world-famous masterpieces with rarely seen works. Exhibition on Screen will bring these stunning works and the incredible story behind them to cinemas around the world while the exhibition is still running, bringing this truly global artist to a global audience. This will be an unmissable chance to get to know this visually spectacular artist and the influence he has had on those who followed.

title: Haunted Wine Tour & Tasting
location: Buena Vista Historical Winery
description:
This fall, Buena Vista Winery invites you to uncover the mysteries, legends, and ghostly encounters woven into more than 165 years of history. Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.
