title: THIRSTY THURSDAY New Member Social for Sonoma County Women's Wine Club
description:
Sonoma County Women's Wine Club (SCWWC)
This is our regular club meeting, held on the last Thursday of every month except for holidays and we are super excited! Come join us at 4th Street Cellars in downtown Santa Rosa. They have generously offered to host our monthly THIRSTY THURSDAY social for us.

If you are new to the area, or just looking to get out of the house and make new friends, this is the place for you. Welcoming to ALL new and (ahem, old) members.

Wine is purchased by the glass for a set fee of $13/$14 per glass with the variety of white, rosé, and red wines offered through 4th Street Cellars which includes tip. Fees are collected at the venue by Co-organizer Daima Phipps via cash, Venmo, or Paypal. You are welcome to purchase wine separately if you choose. Starting March 2025, we ask that every attending member pay a $1 "slush" fund fee per event so that we can build up our funds for club-related expenses, which can be paid by Venmo or cash.

There is no food offered, but you are welcome to bring an appetizer or snack to share with the group, and many ladies do. We will have time to socialize while tasting in the room upstairs to the left or the outside patio if the weather is nice.

The space has a 25 person attendee limit, but the list is open to 40 to eliminate a waitlist, and guests are welcome! Please RSVP below only if you are able to make it, we have an attendance policy: if you No-Show to three events, you may not attend events for the next three months. Please put this event in your calendar so you don't miss out or get dinged. A No-Show is when you are on the 'Going' list, but do not show up.

See you there, ready to kickoff!

description:
Schnucks Wine Dinner with Jeff Bundschu

We invite you to join Jeff Bundschu at Schnucks Des Peres in St. Louis MO on Wednesday October 28th from 6-9pm for a special wine dinner. It will be a culinary experience you won’t want to miss, delicately paired with exceptional wines and their friendly staff.

FROM THE HOST

Join us for an exclusive five-course culinary journey featuring the exceptional cool-climate estate wines of Gundlach Bundschu, Sonoma’s oldest continuously family-owned winery. The evening features sixth-generation vintner and special guest Jeff Bundschu, who will share his personal stories, deep-rooted passion, and distinctively vibrant approach to California winemaking. As each meticulously paired course unfolds, you will gain firsthand insight into the unique terroir of their historic Rhinefarm estate, their sustainable wine-growing philosophies, and the meticulous crafting process that has defined the Bundschu family legacy for nearly 170 years.

title: Samba no Pé - First Class
location: 4140 Redwood Highway #8
description:
Get ready to feel the rhythm and energy of Rio de Janeiro! Samba no Pé \(Samba in the Foot\) is the captivating solo style of samba danced in the streets and at Carnival, known for its rapid, intricate footwork and infectious hip movements.

You will learn

The Basic Step: You will master the signature quick-quick-slow rhythm that defines Samba no Pé.

Arm & Hip Styling: You will learn how to add the authentic flair, movement, and energy that makes Brazilian samba so captivating.

Technique & Posture: You will receive tips on proper body alignment to help you dance longer, faster, and more safely.

Rhythm & Musicality: You will learn how to connect your movement directly to the irresistible beat of the bateria \(the samba drum section\).

This class is perfect for anyone looking to connect with the vibrant spirit of Brazil, improve coordination, and get a fantastic workout—all while learning the foundational steps of this iconic dance. No partner or prior dance experience is required! Just bring your enthusiasm and comfortable shoes!

Date & Time: Thursdays @6:30PM – 7:30PM

Address: 4140 Redwood Highway \#8 San Rafael, CA

Note: Arrive 10 minutes before. No floor marking shoe soles allowed.

title: Sweeney Todd
location: The Raven Performing Arts Theater
description:
Sweeney Todd is largely considered one of Stephen Sondheim’s masterpieces. With it, he aimed to create a musical that could “scare the hell out of everyone,” and yet, somehow, be funny.

The story centers around Sweeney Todd, an unjustly exiled barber who returns to London, seeking vengeance against the lecherous judge who framed him and ravaged his young wife. The road to revenge leads Todd to Mrs. Lovett, a resourceful proprietress of a failing pie shop, above which, he opens a new barber practice. Mrs. Lovett’s luck sharply shifts when Todd’s thirst for blood inspires the integration of an ingredient into her meat pies that has the people of 19th Century London lining up…and the carnage has only just begun!

\***Content Advisory:** Adult language and violent themes, as well as controversial pie recipes. Recommended for 12+.

Running Time: 2 hours, 40 minutes including one intermission.

title: What We Can Know by Ian McEwan [OPTION 2]
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
***What We Can Know* by Ian McEwan**

**Ed's description**: "It is 2119, and Thomas Metcalfe is a humanities academic expert on the 90 30 era - 1990 to 2030 - when the Derangement accelerated leading eventually to the Inundation which destroyed much of the civilized world with ephemeral archives preserved in mountainous libraries while Nigeria houses ALL digital records. Thomas embarks on a hero's journey to find the long lost but legendary 'Corona for Vivien' recited by the famed poet Francis Blundy for his wife's fiftieth birthday party at an 'immortal night' with literary luminaries in 2014. In this period the STEM colleges have all the best students and facilities while Humanities colleges have the lousiest students and facilities, and Thomas hopes his finding of the corona - a poetic structure usually of seven sonnets but 15 in this case - will spark some life in his dying field. He finds Vivien's memoirs, and the second part of the novel belongs to her."

**Lucinda**: "This book was a mind bender. I never quite knew what was going on until the very end. I believe that’s the whole point. I appreciated McEwan’s views on climate decline and what it might lead to. It was thought provoking (no spoilers). I also found the book a little hard to read as it was quite detailed, and the characters might be considered amoral. There is a lot here."

**Dave**: "Intriguing novel. Pondering the future not about technological change but what will do with the vast amount of saved data. How will we encounter our history and the place for humanities in the future."

**Nancy R**: "I've started on my second reading. There's so much in the book to discuss. One thing is 100 years in the future calling global warming 'the derangement.' brilliant, among others. The story is involving and well written, and is sure to generate lively discussions."

*•* "Sophisticated entertainment of a high order." —*The New York Times*
\*• "\*Brilliantly, and surprisingly, plotted."—*The Washington Post •* "A novelist of consummate skill."—*The Wall Street Journal*
*•* "Elegantly structured and provocative."—*Los Angeles Times*

title: Yoga Vinyasa Krama - Talasana Krama & Pranayama
description:
Nataraja School of Traditional Yoga
All Classes RSVP Only at least 24hrs prior
[[breathprayeryoga@protonmail.com](mailto:breathprayeryoga@protonmail.com)]([mailto:breathprayeryoga@protonmail.com](http://mailto:breathprayeryoga@protonmail.com/)), 707-235-1413
\**For All Classes - Certain injuries & health issues may be contraindicated - Please contact me if you have a concern*
**Talasana Krama (Foundational Sequence) & Pranayama**
**Mondays 9-10:30am - Songbird Cotati - RSVP**
**$25, Discounted Class Passes & Sliding Scale Available**
Fundamental practices for understanding the holistic nature, energetics and Sanskrit yoga philosophy guiding the approach of this comprehensive system. Long time yoga practitioners as well as new students will benefit. Experience the distinction of this system verses other modern yoga/vinyasa practices commonly taught & the traditional & precise use of ujjayi breath as it relates to the Sanskrit parameters, moving with the breath and the importance of the pause. Talasana is a very unique & profound krama initiating & establishing "samasthiti", the steadiness and focus of mind, balanced energy and steadiness of body - with the two feet together, moving from the center, all the major joints and muscles of the body are exercised using arm and hand movements, back bends, side bends, twists, forward bends, squats and balancing foot stretches. The fingers interlaced create a prana circuit as they come together in the repetitive movement over the head. The breath specific movements stretch the diaphragm, psoas, massage the heart and internal organs, clear the lungs, drain the lymphatic system, stimulate the vagus nerve and calm the mind. Energy is created along the spine and central nervous system, and is distributed throughout the nadis and into the entire energy body. Regular practice of Talasana flowers into to ananta samapatti and understanding "stillness in movement".
Class begins with Opening Mantras & Ding Namaskar (Devotional Salutation to the Directional Spheres with Breath & Mantra). Then moves to Tāĺāsana to Savasana then Seated Prānāyāma (Yogic Breathing) including Morning Cleansing Kriyas, Ujjayi, Nadi Shuddi, Samantraka Prānāyāma, Pratyahara, Dharana. May include Specific Mudra (Energetic Bodily Gestures).

In my ongoing Gel-Printing & Collage workshop I want to offer you the opportunity to collage with your handmade papers, starting with an easy project progressing each class to a more challenging one.

title: Introduction to Drawing Portraits From Photos (3 Session Class) — Sebastopol Center For the Arts, California
location: Sebastopol Center for the Arts, 282 S High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472
description:
Introduction to Drawing Portraits From Photos (3 Session Class)

  
    
      
        
          $165.00
        
      
    
  

Introduction to Drawing Portraits from Photos November 4th, 11th, and 18th 6:00-9:00pm $150.00 + $15.00 Materials Fee = $165.00 Age Restricted to 18+ About this class: In this three week course, students will learn and practice observational skills and fundamental drawing techniques while learning the basics of drawing portraits from photographs. Drawing human faces requires the same basic drawing skills that one employs for any subject - observing proportion, flattening shapes, and utilizing line or value to convey volume. But the conceptual weight of human faces tends to intimidate artists. When drawing any subject, the hardest skill is simply learning to see, a skill that anyone can be taught, practice, and hone. This course will focus on the practice of looking, and discovering strategies to find objectivity when rendering portraits. This class is for anyone who wants to practice and advance their drawing skills - beginners, those who haven’t practiced in years, or any artists who just want to learn new techniques and practice their skills with consistent feedback and guidance. Through demonstration, practice, and reflective discussion, this class will explore the foundations of rendering human expression with classical drawing techniques in a low pressure environment. Observational drawing gives all artists a foundation of practical knowledge and skills that infinitely expands the possibilities of what one can create. If your ideas feel limited by your drawing skills, if you feel frustrated or stuck in your painting practice, or if you simply want to start drawing and are looking for a place to start, this is the class for you.About the Instructor: Hannah Day received her BA in Visual Arts with an emphasis on drawing and printmaking from University of San Diego, then attended University of Hawaii at Manoa to receive her MFA in printmaking. Hannah’s etchings have been internationally shown and collected, but her art practice also includes paper cutting, graphite, and watercolor. She has taught all ages in many mediums. These days, Hannah primarily teaches watercolor, observational drawing, and paper cutting. You can view her work at www.hannahdrawstrees.com

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

location: Sebastopol Center for the Arts, 282 S High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472
description:
Holiday Handbuilding

  
    
      
        
          $135.00
        
      
    
  

Holiday Handbuilding Thursdays, November 5th, 12th, and 19th from 6:00-9:00pm $90.00 Attendance Price + $45.00 Clay Fee = $135.00Maximum of 10 students. Class Description: Get ready to deck your halls with handmade charm! Join us for our Holiday Handbuilding Class, where you will create some holiday themed pieces for the season of giving using and refining techniques you’ve already tried. In this festive workshop, you will craft your own seasonal treasures, from customer ornaments and cozy mugs to unique holiday decor and heartfelt gifts - with your hands!  Michael will guide you through numerous demonstrations to help you bring your creative visions to life. Grab a friend, embrace the holiday spirit, and build pieces that will become part of your holiday tradition!About the Instructor: Michael Citrino has had a love affair with clay for over 50 years. After his college experience at California College of Arts and Crafts with Viola Frey and further work at Humboldt State University with Lew Merrick, he ran a stained glass business for 18 years. Michael and his wife left for Turkey in 1991 to teach in International Schools. For 26 years he taught K-12 art, including Ceramics, Drawing, Photography, Design and Sculpture at schools in six different countries. He started clay programs for High School and Middle School students at three of those schools. At four of these schools he offered after school and weekend ceramics sessions for teachers and parents. Michael’s work ranges from the traditional to the experimental and a wide swath in between. His approach to teaching is to help students explore the playful nature of the clay room and nurture a love for the possibilities that medium presents.

title: Yoga Vinyasa & Pranayama
description:
Nataraja School of Traditional Yoga
**Yoga Vinyasa Krama - Thursdays 9-10:30am**
**Songbird Community Healing Center Cotati**
**RSVP ONLY**
Physical Health, Conditioning, Pranic Flow, Vital Energy, Mental Focus & Stillness - through intelligent architecture with the metaphysics of deep conscious breathing & slow motion, yogic breathwork, mantra/sound/vibration, mudra, subtle & contemplative practices.
Yoga Vinyasa Krama is a comprehensive hatha-raja yogic system for purification, developing concentration, neuromuscular fitness and conditioning, refining & mastering the breath, awakening subtle energy and stilling the mind. Based on deep breathing & the subtle movement of prana directed into the cartilage tissue, sinuous musculature, internal organs, nerve pathways and nadis. It has over 700 intelligently sequenced slow, conscious breath powered with precision movement variations with pause (vinyasas), exploring many aesthetic variations of each posture to correctly establish the main asanas while the mind merges with the breath.
Includes the energetics of drishti, pratikriyas, bandha, vaseth, mudra, mantra, surya & ding namaskar with breath & mantra, cleansing kriyas, Himalayan pranayama including including ujjayi variations, heating & cooling breaths, solar, lunar & soli-lunar nadi shuddhi practices, pranava & samantraka pranayama, pratyahara, subtle & contemplative practices in 12 kramas (sequences).
The whole process gradually transforms the body and mind, releasing old patterns of physical and mental tension and dysfunctional patterns of movement, providing tonic, energetic and psychophysiological effects.
This system is presented from the teachings **Srivatsa Ramaswami** learned through his over 33 years of one on one study with **Sri Krishnamacharya** and teachings from a similar **Himalayan method**.
This ongoing class will explore the entire system of 12 Kramas with each class focusing on a particular krama or vinyasas from different kramas & pranayama & dharana practices.
Please practice on an empty stomach. Morning beverage ok but please take it 30min or more before class.
***Certain injuries & health issues may be contraindicated Please contact me if you have a concern***
Knowledge of Ujjayi Breathing recommended
**$25 Drop In, Discounted Class Passes, Sliding Scale Available**
\*\***RSVP Only** Contact Kara @707-235-1413, [breathprayeryoga@protonmail.com](http://sunyogadance@gmail.com%2A%2A/)

title: Take the art of Still Life to new places
location: Rileystreet Art Supply,103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Instructor: Sandra Novia

Dates: Thursdays, Ongoing. This is an ongoing 6-class series. You can start your series anytime.

Time: 11:30am - 1:30pm.

Location : Santa Rosa Store

Fee: $310 for 6 classes. Please check with the instructor for details.


This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. We will expand on those mediums as we move into printmaking, collage, and mosaic to bring your art to life. It's a great class to learn the fundamentals for beginners and for experienced artists that want to try their hand at a new art form you haven't done before.

All levels Welcome.

Let's explore the beautiful art of expressing Art together.


To register for this series, please contact Sandra Novia at: (707) 433-ARTS (2787)

title: Pilot Parallel Pen Demonstration: Doodles to Cadels
description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

location: Sebastopol Center for the Arts, 282 S High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472
description:
Jizo Peace Project: Clay Gathering for Remembrance and Peace, November

  
    
      
        
          $10.00
        
      
    
  

Friday, November 6, 2026; 1:30 – 4:00pmDue to limited capacity, we are asking for a suggested donation of $10 to the Sebastopol Center for the Arts to confirm your attendance. Bring a copy of your receipt at check-in to Painting/Drawing Studio adjacent to Ceramics Studio. Additional donations are welcome at the time of the class to cover rental and expenses for the peace project. Join us for a monthly, heart-centered gathering where we come together to create Jizo guardians out of clay—symbols of compassion, protection, and peace. Rooted in the Buddhist tradition and echoed across many cultures, Jizo figures traditionally honor children and all who have passed, those in transition, and those in distress.This ongoing project is dedicated to remembering those lost to war, with a special focus now on the approximately 19,000 children who have perished in Israel and Gaza in recent years. Through the simple, meditative act of working with clay, we create benevolent beings that will become part of public exhibits and peace sites, offering spaces for reflection, mourning, and hope. Our gatherings conclude with a gentle ritual to honor the lives of these children.Located in the Painting & Drawing Room. The gathering is open to ages 12 - adult, and no prior clay experience is necessary—all clay and basic materials are supplied. Registration is required to participate.Donations are welcome to help cover materials and expenses. More than a class, this is a shared space of warmth and care—an opportunity to tend to our own hearts while taking part in love in action.

description:
Occidental Center for the Arts presents Electric Tumbleweed! One of Sonoma County's finest bands returns for our listening and dancing pleasure.
Tickets are $20/$15 for OCA members. Doors open at 7:30 PM. No dogs. Refreshments available. Free parking.
Get Tickets
Electric Tumbleweed is a psychedelic outlaw country group based in Sonoma County, California. Founded in 2019 by members rooted in bluegrass, country, and psychedelic rock, the music is a hard driving mixture of twangy guitar and psychedelic noise, held together by a steady rhythm section with the cry of pedal steel layered in between it all. Electric Tumbleweed has maintained steady momentum in the Northern California music scene; backing David Nelson (New Riders of the Purple Sage) on multiple occasions; most notably at the Mystic Theater with guest Mark Karan (Ratdog) for a sold out performance. Electric Tumbleweed performed regularly at Phil Lesh’s Terrapin Crossroads as a solo group as well as with Scott Law, Barry Sless (Phil Lesh and Friends) and Dave Zirbel (Sammy Hagar Band) are regular pedal steel players in the group. The band has been invited to play multiple festivals and events including The String Cheese Incident’s Hog Farm Hideaway, Ain’t Necessarily Dead Fest (backing David Nelson). We aim to keep our goals high, and to perform high quality music; focusing on writing and arranging new songs, and booking future tour dates. We are excited to release our debut full-length album in October 2021, which features Sam Bush (New Grass Revival), Barry Sless (Phil Lesh & Friends), and Lester and Dylan Chambers (The Chambers Brothers). The album features the artwork of Stanley Mouse/Jennae Bennett and was engineered and mastered by Grammy winning Oz Fritz (Tom Waits).

title: Returning to the First Mark with Catherine Cruz - November 7th — Sebastopol Center For the Arts, California

description:
Returning to the First Mark with Catherine Cruz - November 7th

Returning to the First Mark November 7th, 2026 - 11:00am-3:00pm Attendance Price: $130.00 Ages 16+In this new workshop we will explore drawing and abstract mark making through play, curiosity, and child-like wonder.Before we learned to write words, we communicated through marks. As children, we drew with curiosity, freedom, and a sense of play - without worrying about getting it "right” and without fear of getting our hands dirty.  We played in the dirt and we made things.  This workshop invites you to reconnect with that creative spirit through abstract mark making and intuitive drawing.Using a variety of drawing tools and materials, we'll explore line, texture, rhythm, and gesture as a personal visual language. Through guided exercises and playful experimentation, you'll discover how letting go of expectations can open the door to greater creativity and self-expression.Whether you're an experienced artist or simply curious about abstract drawing, you'll leave with new techniques, greater confidence, and a renewed sense of creative freedom. No drawing experience is necessary - just a willingness to explore. Returning to the first mark means:→ reconnecting with curiosity→ slowing down and truly seeing→ discovering the language within ordinary things→ responding intuitively→ building something personal through lines and marksParticipant must bring the following:Note: There is no need to buy expensive materials, please consider what you already have.  If you’re missing something, let the instructor know, Sebastopol Center for the Arts has a minimal amount of these supplies available to borrow.Apron or clothing you don't mind getting paint onBlack gesso or black acrylic paintSpray bottle with water Acrylic paint: two or three earthy colors such as burnt umber, raw sienna, or yellow ochre.  If you don’t have these specific colors, no need to purchase them, just bring whatever you haveA small container, like a glass jar, to pour the gesso inA variety of paint brushes (3 to 5) from very thin to thickA container for waterDifferent types of paper to draw on, from small to large sheets.  Examples: recycled book pages, copy paper, drawing pad, newsprint, brown paper bags, vintage papers with or without illustrations but nothing too dark or too busy. Two black pens or markers with different tipsGlue stickScissorsPaper towelsThe class will begin with a talk and a demonstration, so please plan to arrive early to allow time to settle in.A short lunch break will be held from 12:30 to 1:00 PM. Kindly bring your own lunch and beverage.About the instructor: Catherine Cruz is a French-American artist whose work is informed by textures and patterns created by the passing of time and the effects of the natural elements on the built environment. She holds a Bachelor of Science in interior design and she worked in the field of architectural design and green building certification for over 25 years. She has taught collage and mixed media workshops in the Bay Area and in France since 2019, and this is her fifth year at the Sebastopol Center for the Arts. Her studio is located in Sebastopol and she participates in Art Trails Open Studios. You may contact Catherine at beyouartstudio@gmail.com. title: Dublinesque Album Release Party
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental
description:
Don't miss this special evening where we’ll take a musical trip to Dublin with some of the Bay Area’s finest musicians and singers! Eamonn Flynn, Darcy Noonan, Hector Bragado and Felim Egan will dazzle us with their traditional and original "Dublinesque" harmonies. OCA favorites through and through, we're just delighted to bring back this spirited, talented group.
Tickets are $25, $20 for OCA members. Doors open at 6:30 PM. Refreshments available, art gallery open during intermission.
Get Tickets
EAMONN FLYNN & DUBLINESQUE
Eamonn Flynn forges his own brand of Irish soul. The Dublin-born singer-songwriter/pianist got his start with The Commitments, a hit film about an Irish soul band, and has since worked with American blues and R&B stars Elvin Bishop, Maria Muldaur, Evelyn Champagne King, Michael Franti & Spearhead, Zigaboo Modeliste (The Meters), The Ray Charles Project, and many more.
​
Flynn's new quartet DUBLINESQUE brings his deep soul and gospel roots together with the Irish music traditions he was raised on.
​
"Dublinesque is my attempt to recreate the kind of parties we had in my parent's house, growing up in Dublin," explains Flynn. "There'd be neighbours and friends and it would always end up as a sing-song/jam session. Everyone would participate - if you couldn't hold a tune you'd perform a 'recitation' or tell a joke!
​
"There was never any delineation between genres of music - whether it was Irish tunes and ballads, soul music or a Beatles song," he emphasizes.
​
The band brings together three talented Bay Area Irish traditional musicians: fellow Irishman Félim Egan (The Black Brothers) on accordion, local favorite Darcy Noonan on fiddle, and from Basque country, Spain, Hector Bragado on banjo. They are also sometimes joined by special guests. Previous guests have included Glide Memorial Choir, Maria Muldaur, Mary Black, Róisín O, Michael Black, Shay Black, Autumn Rhodes, Margaret Graham and dancers from the Kennelly, Dillon and Whelan Schools of Irish Dance and the Cooley-Keegan Branch of Comhaltas Ceoltóirí.
​
"This is my chance to play with some of my favorite musicians and recreate those parties!" says Flynn.
​
Flynn's latest of three solo albums is 'Anywhere But Home,' celebrating Dublin from his San Francisco pandemic perspective. It received praise and widespread airplay in the US, Canada, Europe and Australia.
"Flynn's songwriting moves with true emotional register across history, folklore and poetry…with grit and true Dublin savvy.” Deirdre Cronin - Irish Music Magazine

Winter Botanicals: Watercolor Workshop (2 Sessions) November 8th and November 15th, 2026 1:00-4:00pm $110.00 + $15.00 Materials Fee = $125.00 Age restricted to 18+About this class: In this two week workshop, students will learn a unique approach to watercolor, intended to address the frustration that many feel with this challenging medium. The class will focus on strengthening one’s observational skills, while learning a watercolor technique that teaches the artist to see value and color. Over the two weeks we will work on 1 painting, progressing through guided steps to build a luminous botanical painting. With a mix of demonstrations and individualized instruction, students of all experience levels will develop new skills and have a meaningful creative experience. Our subject will be seasonal botanicals, the iconic and recognizable plants that decorate our holiday season, such as holly and poinsettias. These subjects are great for beginners and master painters alike; their organic shapes are forgiving drawing subjects, but their beauty can be a muse for life. Instructor Hannah Day is a passionate plant painter and will share her unique approach to rendering botanicals. This class will work from photos, practicing observational drawing, in addition to watercolor technique. Beginning artists and repeat students are welcome.About the Instructor: Hannah Day received her BA in Visual Arts with an emphasis on drawing and printmaking from University of San Diego, then attended University of Hawaii at Manoa to receive her MFA in printmaking. Hannah’s etchings have been internationally shown and collected, but her art practice also includes paper cutting, graphite, and watercolor. She has taught all ages in many mediums. These days, Hannah primarily teaches watercolor, observational drawing, and paper cutting. Participants will explore the process of collage making using magazines images on 5” x 8” canvas, usually cut from mat board or other stiff paper. Heart Stories
, acupuncturist, educator, and Sonoma Coast author Dennis von Elgg explores the fascinating intersection of Traditional Chinese Medicine, modern cardiovascular science, and the stories we carry that shape our lives. Drawing on decades of clinical experience, contemporary medical research, timeless Eastern wisdom, and moments from his own journey, von Elgg invites readers to consider heart disease through an entirely new lens—one that recognizes the intimate relationship between physiology, emotion, stress, memory, and consciousness.
Rather than presenting Eastern and Western medicine as opposing viewpoints,
Heart Stories
reveals the surprising places where they converge. Along the way, readers encounter compelling patient stories, reflections from the author’s own life, practical insights for improving cardiovascular health, and an exploration of the emotional patterns that often accompany illness, resilience, and healing.
Written for both healthcare practitioners and thoughtful readers,
Heart Stories
is an exploration of what it means to heal—not only the physical heart, but the human heart as well. Blending science, philosophy, personal reflection, and clinical wisdom, it offers an invitation to see both health and human experience with fresh eyes.
"Drawing from decades of hard-won clinical experience, von Elgg reframes our tradition while respecting its roots, considering the classics in the context of modern research and cardiovascular therapy. With case studies that read like stories and invitations for us to reflect on both ourselves and our patients, this is one of those books that will make going to work all the more interesting and rewarding."
Dr. Jason D. Robertson - Seattle Institute of East Asian Medicine
"This work bridges the measurable and the mysterious aspects of the heart with remarkable intelligence and humanity. Rooted in both cardiovascular science and Chinese medicine, it offers a rare synthesis — equally rigorous and deeply compassionate. Professor von Elgg offers a beautifully articulated exploration of what it truly means for the heart to be 'well.'"
Dr. Bianca Di Giulio,
L.Ac
.
Author of "Bridging the Gap: Integrative Oncology and the Practice of Traditional Chinese Medicine"
"In 'Heart Stories,' Dennis von Elgg turns his holistic lens towards cardiology while finding deeper meaning and enjoyment in our lives. This book is a written treasure that will inform and delight practitioners and patients alike for many generations to come."
Robyn Adcock, DACM, LAc, CMT, Director of Pediatric Integrative Medicine, UCSF
"It is unusual for a book to give both the EKG and the 神 (shén) equal weight. With clinical clarity and a teacher's warmth, Dennis' book makes the case for psychocardiology and a way to meet the whole of a patient's being. For practitioners working where biomedicine and East Asian medicine meet, it's a thoughtful map of a territory that is too often left unexplored."
Toby Daly, PhD, LAc
Author of An Introduction to Chinese Medicine, The Saam Acupuncture Tradition, and Tracing Our Lineage
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Dennis von Elgg,
L.Ac
., is an acupuncturist, educator, and author who has spent more than three decades exploring the intersection of Traditional Chinese Medicine, modern medical science, and the human experience. Living and practicing on California’s Sonoma Coast, he has dedicated his career to helping patients understand the relationship between emotional well-being, cardiovascular health, and the body’s remarkable capacity to heal.
His debut book,
Heart Stories: An Inner Exploration of Heart Disease and Human Consciousness
, weaves together clinical insight, contemporary research, Eastern philosophy, patient stories, and reflections from his own life to offer a fresh perspective on the Heart—not only as an organ, but as a center of physiology, emotion, and consciousness.
Dennis lives on the Sonoma Coast, where he maintains a private acupuncture practice, teaches, writes, practices yoga, coaches high school baseball, and treasures time with his son.
Through his writing, Dennis hopes to encourage a deeper conversation about healing—one that honors both scientific discovery and the wisdom found in our own lived experience, reminding us that the journey toward health is as much about understanding ourselves as it is about understanding the body.

title: Poetic Medicine: 11/10/26 — Sebastopol Center For the Arts, California
location: Sebastopol Center for the Arts, 282 S High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472
description:
Poetic Medicine: November 10th, 2026

  
    
      
        
          $15.00
        
      
    
  

Poetic MedicineTuesday, November 10th, 4:00-5:30pm The practice of “poem making” offers a means to express the metaphors and meaning of the joys and suffering we experience in ourselves and bear witness to in others. Poetry can be a salve for the heart and soul. It is a way of speaking what is true in our hearts  and is often difficult to access without a creative spark. You do not have to be a "poet" or even a "writer" to allow words and feelings to pour through your pen. Redwing Keyssar has been leading "poetic medicine" sessions through her work in Palliative Care at UCSF for the past 6 years. Her work has created an international community of people who, by listening to and writing poetry together, have healed wounds of grief and loss, helped "wounded healers," and provided resiliency to move forward on our life paths.Writing poetry in community is a bit like attending a meditation retreat. The instruction for most beginners when learning to meditate is to simply bring oneself back to the breath, each time the mind wanders. In poem-making, the instruction is to bring oneself back to the heart and along with a deep breath, see if one can open a little bit wider. When we witness each other in this process, in a circle of open-heartedness, something magical happens!This is an IN-PERSON gathering to establish a strong and safe creative community. We are all poets!No Materials Required, Reading Material Provided. Personal writing materials encouraged. 22 students maximum. About the Instructor: Judith Redwing Keyssar, RN has traversed an amazing 35+ year journey in the healing arts/healthcare. Redwing is an educator, end-of-life doula, author, poet, song-writer, ceremonialist, national presenter and frequent contributor to public issues about Palliative and End of Life Care. Redwing is currently the Director of Education at the MERI Center for Education in Palliative Care at UCSF/Mt. Zion. Her professional career includes being the Clinical Director at Zen Hospice Project and the Director of Palliative Care and Nursing at Jewish Family and Children’s Services from 2004-2018. She is a founder and adjunct faculty member of the California State University Shiley/Haynes Institute of Palliative Care, and has taught courses at OLLI at Sonoma State. Redwing is the author of an award-winning book, “Last Acts of Kindness; Lessons for the Living from the Bedsides of the Dying” and is the recipient of numerous awards in the field of Palliative Care. After studying with John Fox at the Institute for Poetic Medicine, her passion for using poetry as a healing modality has led to the development of a successful international program in Poetic Medicine, through her work at the UCSF MERI Center. Learn more about her here: https://redwingkeyssar.com/

description:
2nd & 4th Tuesdays, 2-4 pm in the OCA Lobby
Interested in learning, sharing and reading short plays? Readers Theatre is a fun opportunity to express yourself.
Readers Theatre participants read scripts adapted from literature, while the ‘audience’ pictures the action by hearing the script being read aloud. It requires no sets, costumes, props, or memorized lines. Instead of acting literature as in a play, the performer’s goal is to read a script aloud effectively, enabling the audience to visualize the action. Performers bring the text alive by using voice, facial expressions, and some gestures. $15 participation fee, $10 for OCA members.
Alternating READER’S CHOICE nights: Can be play, poetry, story, essay, your own writing, OR ??????

title: Sound Bath with Laura Benson
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental, CA 95465
description:
Rest & Renew at our Sound Bath!
Support your nervous system, release anxiety and stress, and harmonize your body, mind and spirit on the 2nd Tuesday of every month! Laura Benson has a Masters in Intuition Medicine(R) and is a certified sound healer who will guide you through a gentle meditation before each sound bath session. Bring your own yoga mat & blanket and come ready to rest and renew! In the OCA Studio.
Sliding scale pricing $25-$35.
Register
A sound bath is a whole-body, immersive listening experience. During a sound bath, participants often sit or lie down, and are surrounded by the mostly non-melodic soundscapes created by a range of instruments played by the sound bath facilitator. Hence, they are “bathed” in sound.
Sound therapy is a non-invasive healing modality that utilizes the physical and physiological interactions of sound on our bodies and nervous systems to produce therapeutic results. In a sound healing session, specific sonic frequencies are used to soothe the central nervous system, calm the breath, and quiet the mind by encouraging the brain to move into more relaxed states, down from beta (fight-or-flight) and into theta and alpha waves. This increases present-moment awareness and reduces stress and anxiety. Sound baths have been found to be effective in improving mood, cognitive function, and overall mental, physical, and spiritual wellbeing.
Crystal bowl sound baths are particularly powerful in that each bowl is tuned to a specific frequency that corresponds with a different chakra, or energy center, of the body. Based on specific needs, a practitioner can focus on releasing tension or clearing out stuck energy in specific chakras by playing certain bowls or intervals.
While attending a sound bath, you may experience physical sensations brought out by the crystal sound bowls or gong, such as tingling in your limbs or scalp, slowing of your breathing, eye flutters, or small muscle spasms. Not to worry! These sensations often indicate the release of tension or emotional energy stored in the body’s energy systems.

This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

title: Take the art of Still Life to new places
location: Rileystreet Art Supply,103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Instructor: Sandra Novia

Dates: This is a 6-class series, meeting 6 Fridays: October 30th, November 6th, 13th, 20th, 27th & December 4th.

Time: 2:30pm - 4:30pm.

Location : Santa Rosa Store

Fee: $310 for 6 classes.

This class is an ongoing series. You can register and start at anytime. Please contact instructor for more details.

This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. We will expand on those mediums as we move into printmaking, collage, and mosaic to bring your art to life. It's a great class to learn the fundamentals for beginners and for experienced artists that want to try their hand at a new art form you haven't done before.

All levels Welcomed.

Let's explore the beautiful art of expressing Art together.


To register for this series, please contact Sandra Novia at: (707) 433-ARTS (2787)

location: Rancho Nicasio, 1 Old Rancheria Rd, Nicasio, CA, 94946, United States
description:
Dinner Show with BIG BROTHER & THE HOLDING COMPANY

Big Brother & The Holding Company are considered, along with the Grateful Dead and Jefferson Airplane, the pioneers of the “San Francisco Sound”. They are also the band that launched the career of Janis Joplin.

They are the band that recorded ‘Cheap Thrills’, which has been voted by Rolling Stone as one of the greatest classic rock albums of all time and which, along with their hit version of “Piece of My Heart” is in the Grammy Hall of Fame, and the Library of Congress. Their energy, spirit and their story define a time when music was at the center of a cultural revolution, yet their music is still listened to and loved.

location: Sebastopol Center for the Arts, 282 S High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472
description:
Eco Petals: Crafting a Recycled Bouquet

  
    
      
        
          $70.00
        
      
    
  

Saturday, November 14th, 1:00-4:00pm$60 + $10 Materials feeAges 13+Create a whimsical upcycled bouquet using imagination and an assortment of found and recycled papers. In this playful workshop, you’ll learn simple techniques for shaping paper flowers and combining colors, textures, and unexpected materials. No experience needed—just come ready to explore and leave with a one-of-a-kind handmade bouquet. All supplies provided.About the Instructor: Rendell Hourigan received a BBA in Marketing from Texas Tech University, and has pursued art for over 25 years, focusing on sustainable mixed media. She has studied with artists including Chery Baird, Jenny London, and Teri Sloat, exploring drawing, collage, and soft pastels. Her training includes workshops and courses in art journaling, mosaics, and mark-making. She’s exhibited work at the Sebastopol Center for the Arts, The Graton Gallery, and her SOFA district studio. Drawn to the beauty of discarded materials and passionate about recycling, she incorporates reclaimed materials into her work and now leads art workshops to inspire eco-conscious creativity in others.

title: Whistler by Ann Patchett [OPTION 1]
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
***Whistler*** by Ann Patchett. If you rely on library copies, reserve ASAP as there's a long wait list. \*\**We're scheduling this book early in the month - 2nd and 3rd Sat. - to avoid Thanksgiving weekend.\*\**

PUBLISHER'S DESCRIPTION: "When Daphne Fuller and her husband Jonathan visit the Metropolitan Museum of Art, they notice an older, white-haired gentleman following them. The man turns out to be Eddie Triplett, her former stepfather, who had been married to her mother for a little more than year when Daphne was nine. Now 53, Daphne hasn’t seen Eddie for many years, not since the fateful event that changed the direction of both their lives. Meeting again, time falls away; while their relationship was brief, it had a profound impact on them both, and now that they are reunited, they have no intention of ever being separated again.

"*Whistler* is a story about two adults looking back over the choices they made, and the choices that were made for them. It’s a story about bravery, memory, the often small yet consequential moments that define our lives, and the endless stream of loss that in time comes for us all. Beautiful in its simplicity, it is ultimately about how love endures, and how the feeling of being known by one other person, even for a short period of time, can change everything."

"This exquisite writer has once again delivered an incandescent work of fiction — sweet, but never sentimental, infinitely wise and suffused with love. It’s also an ode to New York City itself…. While Patchett has clearly drawn on actual events and individuals to produce this luminous work, she exhibits the expert novelist’s knack for following a plot where the imagination takes it.... I didn't want it to end." - Leigh Haber, ***The Los Angeles Times***

“Ann Patchett’s new novel is a rare phenomenon in contemporary fiction: a novel both majestic and intimate, original and masterful in its structure, crystalline in its prose, revelatory in its insights, utterly devastating yet ultimately uplifting in its emotional impact. . . . I think it is her best novel yet.” - Priscilla Gilman, ***The Boston Globe***

"Ann Patchett’s new novel, *Whistler*, is that loveliest of summer gifts, a story of reconciliation, of old affections renewed, of a family’s circumference enlarged. Fans of the author’s previous work will open these pages like an old shoebox of family photos. Newcomers — how I envy them those first moments — will discover a writer of gentle wit and quiet grace." - **Ron Charles**

**Christine**: "Just finished listening to this book and absolutely loved it! If you are interested, please listen to the Audible, read by Patchett, who is an excellent narrator. I've already recommended it to a number of friends. BIG thumbs' up! Would definitely read it again."

**Nancy S**: "I liked *Whistler* a lot. Mostly it hit some personal spots with characters just like people I know and situations I have been in. It is Anne Patchett in her most comfortable place— family type relationships, reevaluated, and transformed and just about always for the better."

title: Museum Reception -Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
location: Multicultural Museum - Santa Rosa Campus
description: In early May 2026, we put out a call for nominations, asking for Native American women to represent their Nations, their stories, and their strength through a powerful portrait exhibition celebrating identity, cultural legacy, and the resilience of Native women. We received far more nominations than we expected. Choosing from so many incredible women whose stories deserve to be told was not easy. Every single entry showed us how beautiful and unique and strong Native American women are.  The idea for the Standing in Her Power exhibit was conceived in the Fall of 2025 by student employee Julian Cook, who wanted to showcase photos of Native American women wearing regalia. Through Julian's connections in the Bay Area, the project has grown and led to an exciting collaboration with photographer Alexa Treviño. Cook continues to push the exhibit forward through deep conversations with the participants in order to add personal statements about personal power and growth to the photographs.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website. (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame)

title: Gradina - Balkan Music
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental
description:
Gradina is a Balkan music ensemble based in California’s North Bay area.
We celebrate the seasons and their festivals through song and dance, bringing Old World rituals to new light and new generations to revel in the staying power of gratitude for life on Earth.
We sing both a cappella and with instrumental accompaniment. We lean toward traditional songs and arrangements. We present “sit-down” concerts for choral listening as well as dance concerts, and we are also available to teach most of the dances we present. We are honored to play with many Balkan musicians from near and far, and every concert is different, often with a different array of performers alongside the core group.
Our special guests will be Gaelen Genetti on Bulgarian kaval and Christina Penrose on clarinet.
Tickets are $25/$15 for OCA members. Doors open at 6:30 PM.

title: The Art of Acrylics
description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson
Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

Suzanne's artwork ranges from portraits, figurative genre, landscapes and caricatures. She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

For enrollment and supply list, please text or call Suzanne Carson at 707 888 2083

title: Beginning Watercolor Class
location: Rileystreet Art Supply,1138 4th St, San Rafael, CA 94901, USA
description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes
  * Days & Times: Wednesdays & Fridays, 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM
  * SAN RAFAEL LOCATION ONLY

Learning Objectives:

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools
  * Master the ‘wet on wet’ watercolor technique
  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process
  * Create and label a swatch of colors
  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work
  * Navigate the entire painting process, from choosing colors to building layers

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work
  * Creating solid underdrawings
  * Applying wet-on-wet techniques

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

For more information or to register for this class, please contact Eva at: evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com

You can also visit Eva's website at: http://evamautner.com http://evamautner.com evamautner.com

title: Give 'Em the Arrow Again!  Ladies Night at the Archery Range
description:
Sonoma County Women's Wine Club (SCWWC)
I'm super excited to be able to offer another ladies' Archery night in Santa Rosa! If you've ever had a curiosity about archery, this is your chance to find out more with a fun, interactive lesson.

We have reserved a special event with the indoor range on a Wednesday evening. It will consist of a basic lesson, and then we all get to practice shooting. Everyone will get ample time to practice, as they have many lanes.

This event is focused on a less-competitive, relaxed, and entertaining atmosphere. All skill levels are encouraged. All equipment is provided by them, and we will probably get about an hour or hour and a half to practice.

I encourage everyone to bring a bottle of wine or a snack to share with the rest of the group (We usually end up with a lovely charcuterie and wine spread for everyone to enjoy). Closed toe shoes recommended.

There are 17 spots available, guests welcome.

The ladies' group lesson and event is $31 per person, with $6 prepaid via Paypal and $25 paid to the range.

Please only RSVP 'Yes' if you are able to make it, hostess Dai Phipps will be collecting a $6 fee via Paypal to hold your spot. Paypal/Meetup should lead you to make your payment after you RSVP 'Yes'.

There is an attendance policy for all our events: if you No-Show to three events, you may not attend events for the next three months. Please put this event in your calendar so you don't miss out or get dinged. A No-Show is when you are on the 'Going' list, but do not show up.

Cheers, and hope to see you there!

title: Take the art of Still Life to new places
location: Rileystreet Art Supply,103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Instructor: Sandra Novia

Dates: Thursdays, Ongoing. This is an ongoing 6-class series. You can start your series anytime.

Time: 11:30am - 1:30pm.

Location : Santa Rosa Store

Fee: $310 for 6 classes. Please check with the instructor for details.


This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. We will expand on those mediums as we move into printmaking, collage, and mosaic to bring your art to life. It's a great class to learn the fundamentals for beginners and for experienced artists that want to try their hand at a new art form you haven't done before.

All levels Welcome.

Let's explore the beautiful art of expressing Art together.


To register for this series, please contact Sandra Novia at: (707) 433-ARTS (2787)

title: Pilot Parallel Pen Demonstration: Doodles to Cadels
description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

title: THIRSTY THURSDAY New Member Social for Sonoma County Women's Wine Club
description:
Sonoma County Women's Wine Club (SCWWC)
This is our regular club meeting, held on the last Thursday of every month except for holidays and we are super excited! Come join us at 4th Street Cellars in downtown Santa Rosa. They have generously offered to host our monthly THIRSTY THURSDAY social for us.

If you are new to the area, or just looking to get out of the house and make new friends, this is the place for you. Welcoming to ALL new and (ahem, old) members.

Wine is purchased by the glass for a set fee of $13/$14 per glass with the variety of white, rosé, and red wines offered through 4th Street Cellars which includes tip. Fees are collected at the venue by Co-organizer Daima Phipps via cash, Venmo, or Paypal. You are welcome to purchase wine separately if you choose. Starting March 2025, we ask that every attending member pay a $1 "slush" fund fee per event so that we can build up our funds for club-related expenses, which can be paid by Venmo or cash.

There is no food offered, but you are welcome to bring an appetizer or snack to share with the group, and many ladies do. We will have time to socialize while tasting in the room upstairs to the left or the outside patio if the weather is nice.

The space has a 25 person attendee limit, but the list is open to 40 to eliminate a waitlist, and guests are welcome! Please RSVP below only if you are able to make it, we have an attendance policy: if you No-Show to three events, you may not attend events for the next three months. Please put this event in your calendar so you don't miss out or get dinged. A No-Show is when you are on the 'Going' list, but do not show up.

See you there, ready to kickoff!

title: Prescription for Poetry  — Sebastopol Center For the Arts, California
location: Sebastopol Center for the Arts, 282 S High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472
description:
Prescription for Poetry - November 20th, 2026

  
    
      
        
          $45.00
        
      
    
  

Friday, November 20th, 2026 1:00-5:00pm Fee for this session: $45.00 Prescription for Poetry: A Deeper Dive into Poetic Medicine in Community As a Source of HealingSince March 2025, Redwing Keyssar has been leading monthly Poetic Medicine sessions at Sebastopol Center for the Arts, gathering a vibrant community of folks who listen to an write poems together, as a deeply meaningful source of healing, inspiration and connection. Many people return each month, and new folks come and go as well. There has been a yearning for more time to do this work together in community, to have time and space to delve deeper into the thoughts and feelings that emerge and surprise us, as we hold silence together, as well as listen deeply and write effortlessly. And so… we are now offering a seasonal 4-hour Poetic Medicine Session, beginning on Friday, November 20th, from 1:00-5:00pm!What to Bring: your pen/paper/journal/laptop your water bottle your open heart, be ready to be surprised! Some light snacks will be provided. As with the monthly sessions: The practice of “poem making” offers a means to express the metaphors and meaning of the joys and suffering we experience in ourselves and bear witness to in others. Poetry can be a salve for the heart and soul. It is a way of speaking what is try in our hearts and is often difficult to access without a creative spark. You do not have to be a “poet” or even a “writer” to allow words and feelings to pour through your heart and your pen. About the instructor: Redwing Keyssar, RN, Poet, Author, has been leading “poetic medicine” sessions through her work in Palliative Care at the UCSF MERI Center for Humanity in Healthcare for the past 6 years. Her work has created an international community of people who, by listening to and writing poetry together, have healed wounds of grief and loss, helped “wounded healers”, and provided resiliency to move forward on our life paths. Writing poetry in community is a bit like attending a meditation retreat. The instruction for most beginners when learning to meditate is to simply bring oneself back to the breath, each time the mind wanders. In poem-making, the instruction is to bring oneself back to the heart and along with a deep breath, see if one can open a little bit wider. When we witness each other in this process, in a circle of open-heartedness, something magical happens! Come find the magic in yourself and in the community, and join us for Prescription for Poetry on Friday, November 20th, at 1:00pm.

description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
***Whistler*** by Ann Patchett. If you rely on library copies, reserve ASAP as there's a long wait list. \*\**We're scheduling this book early in the month - 2nd and 3rd Sat. - to avoid Thanksgiving weekend.\*\**

PUBLISHER'S DESCRIPTION: "When Daphne Fuller and her husband Jonathan visit the Metropolitan Museum of Art, they notice an older, white-haired gentleman following them. The man turns out to be Eddie Triplett, her former stepfather, who had been married to her mother for a little more than year when Daphne was nine. Now 53, Daphne hasn’t seen Eddie for many years, not since the fateful event that changed the direction of both their lives. Meeting again, time falls away; while their relationship was brief, it had a profound impact on them both, and now that they are reunited, they have no intention of ever being separated again.

"*Whistler* is a story about two adults looking back over the choices they made, and the choices that were made for them. It’s a story about bravery, memory, the often small yet consequential moments that define our lives, and the endless stream of loss that in time comes for us all. Beautiful in its simplicity, it is ultimately about how love endures, and how the feeling of being known by one other person, even for a short period of time, can change everything."

"This exquisite writer has once again delivered an incandescent work of fiction — sweet, but never sentimental, infinitely wise and suffused with love. It’s also an ode to New York City itself…. While Patchett has clearly drawn on actual events and individuals to produce this luminous work, she exhibits the expert novelist’s knack for following a plot where the imagination takes it.... I didn't want it to end." - Leigh Haber, ***The Los Angeles Times***

“Ann Patchett’s new novel is a rare phenomenon in contemporary fiction: a novel both majestic and intimate, original and masterful in its structure, crystalline in its prose, revelatory in its insights, utterly devastating yet ultimately uplifting in its emotional impact. . . . I think it is her best novel yet.” - Priscilla Gilman, ***The Boston Globe***

"Ann Patchett’s new novel, *Whistler*, is that loveliest of summer gifts, a story of reconciliation, of old affections renewed, of a family’s circumference enlarged. Fans of the author’s previous work will open these pages like an old shoebox of family photos. Newcomers — how I envy them those first moments — will discover a writer of gentle wit and quiet grace." - **Ron Charles**

**Christine**: "Just finished listening to this book and absolutely loved it! If you are interested, please listen to the Audible, read by Patchett, who is an excellent narrator. I've already recommended it to a number of friends. BIG thumbs' up! Would definitely read it again."

**Nancy S**: "I liked *Whistler* a lot. Mostly it hit some personal spots with characters just like people I know and situations I have been in. It is Anne Patchett in her most comfortable place— family type relationships, reevaluated, and transformed and just about always for the better."

description:
Instructor: Jan Lochner
Date: Saturday, November 21st
Time: 2:00PM-5:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Fee: $40.00

This is a hands-on make and take class where you will make at least five items including a bookmark, a greeting card, a fridge magnet and an ornament. The class will use two different techniques and Jan will explain how to press flowers and which flowers hold their color best. It is a creative experience!


To register for this workshop, please contact Jan at: mailto:freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com mailto:freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com

Creating note cards from pressed flowers has been Jan’s hobby for 25 years, though she has no formal art training. She utilizes color,
shape and texture on fine quality paper, each card uniquely handmade. Jan’s home in Sebastopol is her studio: the dining room table is her workshop, the kitchen cupboards storing boxes and trays of flowers. She buys card stock by the thousand and picks blooms from her garden and other public places. Her family is used to me saying, “could we stop for just a few minutes so I can gather some… ”

It is a wonderful way of life.

*A note to all students: Please park on in the East facing parking lot while attending classes. We greatly appreciate it. Thank you.

title: The Art of Acrylics
description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson
Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

Suzanne's artwork ranges from portraits, figurative genre, landscapes and caricatures. She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

For enrollment and supply list, please text or call Suzanne Carson at 707 888 2083

title: Beginning Watercolor Class
location: Rileystreet Art Supply,1138 4th St, San Rafael, CA 94901, USA
description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes
  * Days & Times: Wednesdays & Fridays, 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM
  * SAN RAFAEL LOCATION ONLY

Learning Objectives:

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools
  * Master the ‘wet on wet’ watercolor technique
  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process
  * Create and label a swatch of colors
  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work
  * Navigate the entire painting process, from choosing colors to building layers

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work
  * Creating solid underdrawings
  * Applying wet-on-wet techniques

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

For more information or to register for this class, please contact Eva at: evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com

You can also visit Eva's website at: http://evamautner.com http://evamautner.com evamautner.com

title: Take the art of Still Life to new places
location: Rileystreet Art Supply,103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Instructor: Sandra Novia

Dates: Thursdays, Ongoing. This is an ongoing 6-class series. You can start your series anytime.

Time: 11:30am - 1:30pm.

Location : Santa Rosa Store

Fee: $310 for 6 classes. Please check with the instructor for details.


This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. We will expand on those mediums as we move into printmaking, collage, and mosaic to bring your art to life. It's a great class to learn the fundamentals for beginners and for experienced artists that want to try their hand at a new art form you haven't done before.

All levels Welcome.

Let's explore the beautiful art of expressing Art together.


To register for this series, please contact Sandra Novia at: (707) 433-ARTS (2787)

title: Pilot Parallel Pen Demonstration: Doodles to Cadels
description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

title: Take the art of Still Life to new places
location: Rileystreet Art Supply,103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Instructor: Sandra Novia

Dates: This is a 6-class series, meeting 6 Fridays: October 30th, November 6th, 13th, 20th, 27th & December 4th.

Time: 2:30pm - 4:30pm.

Location : Santa Rosa Store

Fee: $310 for 6 classes.

This class is an ongoing series. You can register and start at anytime. Please contact instructor for more details.

This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. We will expand on those mediums as we move into printmaking, collage, and mosaic to bring your art to life. It's a great class to learn the fundamentals for beginners and for experienced artists that want to try their hand at a new art form you haven't done before.

All levels Welcomed.

Let's explore the beautiful art of expressing Art together.


To register for this series, please contact Sandra Novia at: (707) 433-ARTS (2787)

title: Laurie Lewis and the Right Hands
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental
description:
Bluegrass and American Roots Music
Don't miss this incredible show at OCA! Bluegrass legend Laurie Lewis and her amazing band The RIght Hands will give us an afternoon show that you won't soon forget. Laurie will be joined by Brandon Godman, Hasee Ciaccio and other fine musicians for this performance.
Tickets are $35, $30 for OCA members. Doors open at 2:30 PM. Refreshments available, free parking. Art gallery open during intermission. ADA seating available - please contact us at
info@occidentalcenterforthearts.org
for details.
Get Tickets
For nearly four decades, Laurie Lewis has gathered fans and honors for her powerful and emotive voice and her versatile, dynamic songwriting. She is a sought-after recording producer and an equally skilled teacher and mentor.
And she is an inspiration and a ground-breaker – across genres, across geography and across gender barriers.
Laurie has shown us how a woman can blend into any part of the classic bluegrass singing trio, and she showed us how a great voice could move fluidly between bluegrass and other types of music. She showed us how a female fiddler could emulate the strength and grit of the early bluegrass musicians. She has shown how a Californian can appeal to traditional bluegrass audiences, as well as winning acclaim in the worlds of Americana and folk music.
She has shown us how to lead bands of talented musicians – learning from them while helping them make their best music. And she has shown us how to thrive in a constantly changing musical environment – without ever sacrificing her art.
"Her voice is a rare combination of grit and grace, strength and delicacy. Her stories always ring true."
Linda Ronstadt

title: Reflections on Suffering
description:
Rosicrucians AMORC, Santa Rosa, CA
Topic:
**Reflections on Suffering**
**Atrium Group Convocation presented by Frank Nappi, F.R.C.**

In this message we learn that as students on the mystical path we should regard every painful experience as a lesson and determine to use it when progressing on the road towards wisdom. Every event in our earthly life contributes to our inner evolution. That is why every step we take in our life’s journey leads us towards greater understanding and awakens in us knowledge of one’s self.

All AMORC members, their families and friends of the Rosicrucian Order are welcome to attend. We are delighted to have you join us in this inspiring ritual.

• Important to know- Doors open for members and non-member friends of the Rosicrucian Order by 6:30 PM. Please arrive early! The Atrium Group ritual begins promptly at 7:00 PM. AMORC Members - please bring your Active member credentials or Active membership dues receipt.

Following the meeting:
1st Tuesday- Mystical Seekers Series Public Presentation at 8:00 PM

As always, our events are free, and donations are gratefully accepted to help defray our costs.

The Santa Rosa Pronaos is a 501c3 educational non-profit, an affiliated body of the Rosicrucian English Grand Lodge for the Americas and the Caribbean.
